Description: The 2026 MV Agusta Brutale 800 continues to embody the brand's iconic blend of minimalist aggression, premium components, and thrilling performance, positioning itself as a highly desirable entry point into the MV Agusta universe. At its heart lies the signature 798cc triple-cylinder engine, now optimized to meet the latest Euro 5+ emission standards while maintaining a spirited output of 112 hp and 85 Nm of torque, complete with a counter-rotating crankshaft for enhanced agility. The bike features a high-performance steel trellis frame, a fully adjustable Marzocchi/Sachs suspension setup, and upgraded Brembo M4.32 front calipers, affirming its razor-sharp handling credentials. A comprehensive electronics suite is governed by a 6-axis IMU, offering rider aids like cornering ABS and traction control, all accessible via a new 5.5-inch TFT display. The inclusion of the Advanced Connectivity Device with anti-theft and geolocation functions, along with a striking new Rosso Ago Opaco color scheme, ensures the 2026 Brutale 800 remains a beautifully sculpted and technologically advanced Italian streetfighter.

Description: The Hero Hunk 440 2026 is a contemporary, A2-license friendly roadster that marks Hero MotoCorp's push into the premium segment. Essentially a rebadged and updated version of the Mavrick 440, it is powered by a 440cc single-cylinder, air/oil-cooled engine that produces a modest 27 bhp and a healthy 36 Nm of torque at a low 4,000 rpm, emphasizing accessible, unhurried power delivery rather than outright speed. It is built around a tubular steel trellis frame and features a decent components package for its competitive price, including 43mm KYB USD front forks, preload-adjustable twin rear shocks, and dual-channel ABS with ByBre calipers. The bike aims to attract new or younger riders with its nimble handling, comfortable ergonomics (803mm seat height), and modern features like a TFT dash with Bluetooth connectivity for turn-by-turn navigation.

Description: The MV Agusta Enduro Veloce 2026 receives a subtle yet significant upgrade for the 2026 model year, solidifying its position as a premium contender in the adventure segment. At its heart remains the charismatic 931 cc three-cylinder engine, utilizing a counter-rotating crankshaft for exceptional agility and delivering 124 hp with a distinctive MV Agusta soundtrack. For 2026, the factory has enhanced the standard equipment package, now including side panniers, a center stand, new protection bars, and revised fog lights, boosting its touring and off-road readiness straight out of the crate. The Enduro Veloce rolls on new Bridgestone AT41 tires and features a fully adjustable Sachs suspension system with 210mm of travel at both ends, maintaining its blend of on-road precision and off-road capability.

Description:
The newly released Norton Atlas and Atlas GT represent a major milestone in Norton's modern "Resurgence" strategy under parent company TVS, marking the iconic British manufacturer's entry into the competitive middleweight adventure and sport-touring segment. Both motorcycles are built around an all-new 585cc liquid-cooled, DOHC parallel-twin engine with a 270-degree crankshaft, producing 69 bhp at 9,300 rpm and 57.5 Nm of torque at 7,500 rpm. While sharing a lightweight steel trellis frame, a sleek "reductive" design with concealed fixings, and a wet weight of under 200 kg, the two models are engineered for distinct purposes.
The Atlas is designed for off-road and all-terrain adventures, featuring a 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheel setup, 180 mm of KYB suspension travel, higher ground clearance, and an 845 mm seat height.
The Atlas GT is tailored for tarmac-focused touring, equipped with 17-inch street-oriented wheels at both ends, a firmer 140 mm KYB suspension setup, and a lower 815 mm seat height for enhanced on-road handling and rider confidence.
Both models are packed with advanced technology, including an 8-inch touchscreen TFT display with integrated navigation and a comprehensive Bosch six-axis IMU that enables lean-sensitive ABS, traction control, slide control, wheelie control, and cornering cruise control. Higher-spec Apex variants further enhance the package with electronic combined braking, vehicle hold assist, a tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS), heated grips, and adaptive cornering lights. Overall, the Atlas duo blends purposeful British craftsmanship with modern technology, positioning Norton as a serious contender in the highly competitive middleweight adventure and sport-touring market.
specs: KYB 43mm USD forks, 180mm travel, fully adjustable
KYB monoshock RSU, 180mm travel, full hydraulic adjustment

Description:
The Norton Manx R is a modern superbike powered by a 1,200 cc, 72-degree, liquid-cooled V4 engine that produces 206 bhp at 11,500 rpm and 130 Nm of torque at 9,000 rpm. Equipped with a 14.5-liter fuel tank, the Manx R delivers an average fuel economy of approximately 15.6 km/l (around 36.7 mpg or 6.4 L/100 km), providing a real-world riding range of roughly 220 km per tank.
Built around a die-cast aluminum frame with a single-sided swingarm and an 8-inch TFT display, the Manx R lineup comprises four distinct variants, all powered by the same V4 engine:
Manx R (Base Variant): Features a dual-seat configuration, composite bodywork, cast aluminum wheels, and manually adjustable Marzocchi suspension. It has a wet weight (excluding fuel) of 210 kg.
Manx R Apex: Upgrades to semi-active, electronically adjustable Marzocchi suspension and lighter OZ Racing forged aluminum wheels, reducing the weight to 207 kg.
Manx R Signature: Offers a track-focused, single-seat configuration, full carbon-fiber bodywork, and lightweight Rotobox Bullet Pro carbon-fiber wheels. It weighs 203 kg.
Manx R First Edition: Limited to 150 units, this variant features single-seat carbon-fiber bodywork, Rotobox carbon-fiber wheels, titanium fasteners, an Akrapovic titanium exhaust, billet aluminum components, and numbered top yokes. It has a lightweight construction with a claimed weight of just 201 kg.
specs: Norton 72-degree liquid-cooled V4, 1200cc. Chain-driven cams with idler gear for reduced engine height. Titanium inlet valves
Marzocchi 45mm USD chromed inner tubes, 120mm travel, full manual adjustment, passive damping
Marzocchi monoshock RSU, 126mm travel, full manual adjustment, passive damping
2x 320mm semi-floating discs, radially mounted Brembo Hypure 4-piston callipers with Bosch Cornering ABS EVO
245mm disc, 2-piston calliper with Bosch Cornering ABS EVO
463 lbs. (Manx R) / 457 lbs. (Apex) / 448 lbs. (Signature) / 443 lbs. (First Edition)

Description:
The S4 Honcho represents a major shift for LiveWire—Harley-Davidson’s all-electric spinoff—marking its entry into the rapidly growing, lightweight electric "mini-moto" category. Built in partnership with Taiwanese scooter giant KYMCO, this 125cc-equivalent platform strips away the heavy weight and premium pricing of LiveWire's earlier full-sized models to deliver an agile, highly accessible urban runabout. Mechanically, the Honcho features a mid-mounted electric motor utilizing a traditional chain drive to provide a familiar motorcycle feel, capable of hitting a top speed of 59 mph (95 km/h) and sprinting from 0 to 30 mph in a punchy 3.0 seconds. A standout feature for the brand is its dual removable, swappable 3.48 kWh battery packs tucked neatly under the flip-up bench seat, offering a WMTC-estimated range of up to 53 miles (which can stretch past 70 miles during low-speed city cruising) and a 20-to-80% charge time of roughly two hours via a standard household outlet.
The S4 Honcho platform targets two distinct riding lifestyles right out of the gate with its launch variants:
S4 Honcho Street: The fully road-legal urban commuter configuration. It is built for city streets with a 31-inch seat height, basic telescopic forks, 12-inch cast wheels wrapped in street-biased tires, and scooter-style handlebar-actuated linked disc brakes. It comes fully equipped with a 5-inch digital display, mirrors, a license plate bracket, and full LED lighting—making it ready for M-endorsement riders in the US and A1 license holders in Europe.
S4 Honcho Trail: A stripped-down, off-road-only recreational variant. It swaps out the street gear for an extra inch of suspension travel (raising the seat height to 32 inches), beefier handlebars, increased ground clearance, and chunky, knobbier balloon tires designed for dirt tracks. By deleting the headlights, indicators, and mirrors, it sheds weight down to 253 pounds (compared to the Street's 266 pounds). It also curiously features a reverse gear—making it an ideal, license-free option for outdoorsmen, hunters, and weekend trail riders seeking silent propulsion through nature.

The 2027 Yamaha WR125R marks the exciting return of the venerable dual-sport to the brand's lineup, aiming to be a supremely accessible entry point for new riders. At the heart of this "do-it-all" machine is a new 125cc liquid-cooled, SOHC, four-valve single-cylinder engine featuring Variable Valve Actuation (VVA) technology, which is designed to deliver a broad powerband with ample torque at low-to-mid-range RPMs and strong high-end power—a significant upgrade for its class. True to its dual-sport nature, it's built on a semi-double cradle frame with long-travel KYB suspension and dirt-ready 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheels. Beyond its off-road capability, the WR125R includes modern features like a multi-function LCD dash with smartphone connectivity via the Y-Connect app, LED lighting, and front-wheel single-channel ABS.
specs: Overall length x width x height

Description: Zero Motorcycles is shaking things up with the 2026 Zero LS1 electric scooter, designed specifically for urban commuters. This stylish and practical scooter is part of Zero's "All-Access" initiative, aiming to make electric two-wheelers more approachable. The scooter features a center-mounted motor and a standard configuration with dual removable batteries housed in the floorboard, providing a claimed range of approximately 115 km (72 miles). For extended trips, an optional third battery can be installed in the under-seat storage to boost the total range to an impressive 173 km (108 miles). With a top speed of 100 km/h (62 mph), standard ABS and traction control, and flexible charging options including an optional fast charger, the LS1 is clearly engineered for the demands of city life.

The newly released Suzuki SV-7GX 2026 marks an exciting evolution of Suzuki’s legendary middleweight platform, blending sporty road performance with long-distance touring comfort. Inspired by the larger GSX-S1000GX, the SV-7GX features aggressive crossover styling, an upright riding position, adjustable windscreen, LED lighting, and a modern 4.2-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity. Power comes from an updated 645cc Euro5+ compliant V-twin engine producing around 73 PS and 64 Nm of torque, paired with a six-speed gearbox and bi-directional quickshifter for a smoother, more refined riding experience. Suzuki has also equipped the bike with advanced rider aids including ride-by-wire throttle, selectable riding modes, traction control, and the Suzuki Intelligent Ride System (S.I.R.S.), making it a highly versatile machine for commuting, touring, and spirited weekend rides alike.
specs: Link type, coil spring, oil damped, spring preload adjustable

Description: The Hero Vida VX2 Plus 2026 is a game-changer in the electric scooter market, offering a blend of performance, convenience, and technology for urban commuting. With its impressive range of 142 km and top speed of 80 kmph, it's perfect for daily rides. The scooter features removable batteries, making it super convenient to charge at home or office, and comes with smart features like an all-digital console, multiple riding modes (Eco, Ride, and Sport), keyless control, and smartphone connectivity. Its stylish, modern design and compact proportions make it a top contender in the competitive electric scooter market, rivaling models like the Ather and Ola.

The Skygo Bolt 150 2026 is positioned as an affordable maxi-scooter, aiming to offer a blend of style, comfort, and practical features for urban commuters and enthusiasts on a budget. It is powered by a 149cc single-cylinder, liquid-cooled, four-stroke engine with Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI), delivering modest but adequate power for city riding, typically around 13 horsepower. The scooter is known for its modern aesthetics, which draw inspiration from more premium maxi-scooter designs, and it comes equipped with contemporary features such as a digital display, LED head- and tail-lamps, and a pass-light switch. For safety and convenience, it includes front and rear disc brakes and a side-stand kill-switch. With a low seat height of 760 mm and a generous 13-liter fuel tank, the Bolt 150 balances accessibility for various riders with a decent range for daily commutes.

The 2026 Can-Am Renegade lineup solidifies its position as the industry's most aggressive and powerful sport ATV, offering riders a selection of high-performance models designed to conquer any terrain. Core to the lineup are the powerful Rotax V-twin engines, including the range-topping 91 hp 1000R (976cc) and a capable 650 version producing 62 hp, both featuring Intelligent Throttle Control (iTC) with selectable riding modes (Standard, ECO, Sport). All models benefit from a significant suspension upgrade, featuring an innovative front double-arched A-arm design for a wider stance and improved clearance. The high-performance variants, the trail-ready Renegade X xc 1000R and the mud-dominating Renegade X mr 1000R, come equipped with premium FOX PODIUM shocks and Tri-Mode Dynamic Power Steering (DPS). The X mr 1000R further specializes for deep mud with a snorkeled engine/CVT, a robust 3,500-lb winch, and large, aggressive 30-inch ITP Cryptid tires with Visco-4Lok front differential, while the X mr 650 offers similar mud-focused features with the class-leading 650cc V-twin. The entire 2026 Renegade family is built for riders who demand uncompromising power, agility, and armored-up protection for intense off-road adventures.

Description:
The Yamaha EC-06 2026 is Yamaha’s newly released electric scooter aimed at urban commuters, blending practicality with modern technology. It is powered by a 4 kWh fixed lithium-ion battery paired with an efficient Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) that produces around 6.7 kW (9 hp) of peak power and 26 Nm of torque, giving it a top speed of about 79 km/h and a certified range of up to 169 km on a single charge—enough for most city riding needs. Charging from a standard home socket takes roughly eight hours, and Yamaha backs the battery with a 3-year/30,000 km warranty.
In terms of features, the EC-06 sports full LED lighting, a colour LCD instrument cluster with connectivity via the Yamaha Motor Connect R app, and three selectable riding modes (Eco, Standard, Power) plus a handy reverse mode for easy manoeuvring in tight spaces. It also offers disc brakes front and rear with a Combi Brake System (CBS), conventional suspension suited for urban roads, and a 24.5 litre under-seat storage compartment for everyday essentials. The scooter’s clean, contemporary design and tech-friendly features make it a compelling choice in the growing e-scooter segment.
specs: IP67 rating for Motor and Battery IP65 rating for other electronics (IP- Ingress Protection)

Description: The newly launched Yamaha FZ-Rave 2026 is the latest addition to the brand's highly popular FZ family, designed to appeal specifically to young riders seeking a blend of aggressive streetfighter styling and everyday practicality. While mechanically sharing the proven 149cc air-cooled, single-cylinder engine that produces 12.4 PS and 13.3 Nm of torque (mated to a 5-speed gearbox), the Rave distinguishes itself with fresh cosmetic updates. Key aesthetic changes include a bold, new full-LED projector headlamp with an integrated position light and a sculpted fuel tank with cosmetic air vents, giving it a sharper, more muscular look compared to its FZ siblings. Priced competitively, the FZ-Rave aims to offer a balanced package of linear performance, high fuel efficiency, and confident safety with its single-channel ABS system, making it a compelling option in the 150cc premium commuter segment.

The newly released Yamaha Aerox-E marks Yamahas entry into the premium performance electric scooter segment, translating the aggressive, race-inspired maxi-scooter styling of its petrol-powered sibling into a zero-emission platform. Built on a sturdy underbone chassis with 14-inch alloy wheels and wide tires, it retains the signature motorcycle-like high-speed stability and sharp handling characteristics that riders expect from the Aerox lineup. At its core, the Aerox-E is powered by a swingarm-mounted 9.4 kW electric motor producing 48 Nm of torque and reaching a top speed of 95.5 km/h. Power comes from two removable 1.5 kWh lithium-ion batteries, delivering an Indian Driving Cycle (IDC) certified range of up to 117 km. It is equipped with modern features, including a 5-inch color TFT display with turn-by-turn navigation via Y-Connect, a keyless SmartKey system, single-channel ABS, Traction Control, multiple ride modes, and a dedicated 10-second Boost button for quick overtaking. While the under-seat placement of the removable batteries reduces storage space compared to the ICE version, the Aerox-E stands out as a premium, high-tech electric scooter designed for enthusiasts who prioritize sporty styling, connected technology, and dynamic riding performance over everyday utility.

The Scott Fastlane 10 2026 is a high-performance electric road bike that masterfully blends the sleek aesthetics and ride quality of a traditional racing bike with subtle, effective electric assistance. At its core, the bike features an ultra-lightweight HMX carbon frame and is equipped with the compact TQ HPR40 mid-motor drive unit, which provides up to 40 Nm of smooth, natural-feeling torque, powered by a discreet, integrated 290 Wh internal battery. The bike's overall weight is remarkably low, typically around 10.6 kg, making it competitive even with some non-assisted performance bikes. The Fastlane 10 is specced with the Shimano Ultegra Di2 electronic 2x groupset for precise and reliable shifting, complemented by Syncros Capital 1.0 40 Disc wheels and Schwalbe PRO ONE Evo tires. This model is designed for riders seeking speed and efficiency who want the look and feel of a high-end road machine with a gentle, yet powerful boost to conquer climbs and extend their range without the typical bulk of an e-bike.

Description: The QJ Motor SRK 921 RR 2026 represents a bold leap for the Chinese manufacturer into the high-performance litre-class territory, acting as a direct beneficiary of QJ Motor's strategic partnership with MV Agusta. At its heart lies a potent 921cc inline-four engine—derived from the MV Agusta Brutale platform—that churns out approximately 127 horsepower and 93 Nm of torque, offering a raw, high-revving character often missing from modern, emissions-strangled sportbikes. Visually, the machine is striking, featuring aggressive aerodynamic winglets, a single-sided swingarm, and a distinctive quad-exit exhaust that pays clear homage to its Italian lineage. It doesn't cut corners on hardware either; the chassis is equipped with premium components like fully adjustable Marzocchi suspension, Brembo Stylema calipers, and a comprehensive electronics suite that includes a 6-axis IMU, cornering ABS, traction control, and a built-in dashcam.

The newly launched Yamaha Jog E for the 2026 model year marks a significant step in the brand's electric mobility strategy, blending the timeless appeal of the Jog scooter line with modern EV technology. Introduced initially in a limited pre-release in select Japanese markets, the Jog E is a Class 1 moped designed for urban commuting, offering a practical and eco-friendly alternative to its gasoline-powered predecessor. A key feature of this model is its adoption of the swappable Honda Mobile Power Pack e:, leveraging a common battery-sharing infrastructure (like Gachaco in Japan) to eliminate range anxiety and charging wait times. Powered by an in-wheel electric motor, the scooter delivers performance suited for frequent stop-and-go city driving and is capable of a claimed range of 53 kilometers per charge. With user-centric features like an inverted LCD screen, multiple ride modes (Econ, Ready, and Speed), and practical storage including a front USB charging socket, the new Jog E is positioned as a convenient and accessible electric option, with a standard retail package (including the battery and charger) expected for a wider release in the second half of 2026.

The Benelli 180S 2026 is a visually aggressive "naked" streetfighter that brings a premium Italian aesthetic to the entry-level sport bike segment. Designed for urban agility, it is powered by a liquid-cooled, 175.3cc single-cylinder engine featuring a unique triple-spark plug technology (B3SP), which optimizes combustion to deliver a punchy 18 horsepower and 14 Nm of torque through a 6-speed transmission. Its muscular stance is defined by sharp, angular bodywork, an exposed perimeter frame, and a distinctive "alien-face" LED projector headlight that gives it substantial road presence.
Mechanically, it supports this sporty look with inverted (USD) front forks and a rear mono-shock suspension, offering precise handling for city commuting, while front and rear disc brakes ensure reliable stopping power. With a fully digital instrument cluster and fuel efficiency averaging around 40–45 km/L, the 180S serves as an ideal choice for riders seeking a stylish, tech-forward daily commuter that feels larger and more capable than standard 150cc rivals.

specs: 41mm Upside-down forks Marzocchi, compression, recovery, preload adjustable
45mm Central shock absorber with spring preload adjustment and hydraulic rebound brake adjustable
Brembo Dual floating discs, 4-piston caliper with ABS

Description: The newly released Yadea OWIN 2026 electric scooter marks Yadea’s push toward a more premium, tech-forward commuter offering, blending sharp styling with solid real-world practicality. Designed for urban riders, the OWIN features a sleek, aerodynamic body paired with a punchy hub motor that delivers lively acceleration for city traffic. Its battery setup promises an efficient riding range suitable for daily commutes, while fast-charging support keeps downtime low. Modern touches like a fully digital display, keyless start, multiple riding modes, and smart connectivity enhance convenience, and Yadea’s improved chassis tuning ensures a comfortable, stable ride on rough roads.
specs: F: disc brake T: drum brake

Description: The newly launched QJ Motor SRK 1051 RR 2026 marks a bold step for the Chinese manufacturer into the premium liter-class superbike territory, blending accessible performance with striking Italian design. At its heart lies a liquid-cooled, 1,051cc inline-four engine—derived from MV Agusta architecture—that delivers a solid 144 horsepower (106 kW) at 10,600 rpm. While it may not chase the 200-horsepower figures of its European rivals, the SRK 1051 RR distinguishes itself with a focus on usable street performance and high-end componentry, featuring fully adjustable Marzocchi suspension, Brembo Stylema brakes, and a single-sided swingarm that underscores its premium aesthetics. Styled by the Italian studio C-Creative, the bike boasts an aggressive, aerodynamic silhouette and comes equipped with a modern electronics suite, including a TFT display, cornering ABS, traction control, and a quickshifter, positioning it as a compelling, high-value alternative in the sportbike market.

specs: TWIN SHOCK ABSORBER, GAS FILLED EMULSION WITH 5-STEP ADJUSTABLE PRE-LOAD
DISC WITH FLOATING CALIPER AND ABS
DISC WITH FLOATING CALIPER AND ABS

Description: The newly launched Harley-Davidson X440 T emerges as the premium flagship of the X440 line, building upon the foundational success of the standard model with significant upgrades. While retaining the powerful 440cc air-oil-cooled single-cylinder engine that produces 27 BHP and 38 Nm of torque, the 'T' variant introduces modern rider aids with a crucial ride-by-wire throttle. This enhancement unlocks two distinct riding modes—Rain and Road—along with switchable traction control and switchable rear ABS, offering a safer and more engaging ride across varying conditions. Aesthetically, the X440 T sports a notably re-engineered rear subframe and tail section, which, along with new bar-end mirrors and updated graphics, gives the bike a more cohesive, sportier stance reminiscent of the legendary Harley-Davidson XR1200. This combination of classic design, muscular performance, and advanced electronics makes the X440 T a more complete and premium roadster package.

Description:
Yamaha has expanded its legendary supersport lineup with the introduction of the all-new Yamaha YZF-R2 (Yamaha R2), a sharp, performance-oriented motorcycle specifically developed to bridge the gap between entry-level lightweight models like the R15 V4 and larger mid-capacity supersports. Built around a refined diamond-type steel frame optimized for high-speed stability and agile cornering, the R2 captures the aggressive design DNA of Yamaha’s R-series family. It features sharp aerodynamic fairings, integrated winglets, dual-strip LED daytime running lights, and a central LED projector headlamp that mirrors the styling of the R6 and R1.
At its heart is an all-new liquid-cooled, 204cc single-cylinder, DOHC, 4-valve engine paired with a 6-speed gearbox. The engine is engineered to deliver smooth power delivery across the rev range, along with a rev-happy top-end performance ideal for both canyon carving and track days. To ensure riders can harness its power with confidence, Yamaha has equipped the R2 with a robust chassis package comprising 37mm inverted front forks, a link-type rear Monocross suspension, and dual-channel ABS with disc brakes at both ends.
Modern technology is fully integrated into the riding experience, including a 5-inch full-color TFT display with Bluetooth smartphone connectivity for turn-by-turn navigation and call alerts, multi-level traction control, ride-by-wire throttle response with selectable power modes, and an optional bi-directional quickshifter on top-tier trims. Tipping the scales at a nimble 149 kg kerb weight, the Yamaha R2 strikes a balance between track-ready ergonomics and everyday usability, offering dynamic handling, low-end flexibility, and high-spec electronics that make it a compelling upgrade for riders stepping up to dedicated sport bikes.

The QJ Motor SRV 250 is a cruiser-style motorcycle that has garnered attention in various international markets for offering a blend of classic aesthetics and modern components. Powering the bike is a 249 cc, liquid-cooled, V-twin, 4-stroke, 8-valve DOHC engine, which produces a reported maximum power of around 27.5 horsepower at 9,000 rpm and peak torque of 23 Nm at 7,000 rpm, which is a competitive output for its class. The motorcycle often features an Upside-Down (USD) front fork and dual rear shock absorbers for suspension, and braking duties are handled by disc brakes on both ends, complemented by Dual-Channel ABS for enhanced safety. The SRV 250's styling typically includes a low seat height (around 700 mm), a wide rear tire (often 150/80-15), and a digital instrument console. Depending on the market and specific variant (like the SRV 250A), it may also be available with a 6-speed Automatic Manual Transmission (AMT) option, making it an accessible cruiser for a wider range of riders.

The Honda NS150LA 2026 is a stylish, contemporary scooter that blends neo-retro design with modern technology to deliver a sophisticated yet practical urban riding experience. Its aesthetics draw inspiration from the classic ’80s and ’90s “stereo era,” featuring smooth, flowing body lines, rounded headlamps, and distinctive L-shaped LED position lights that evoke the charm of classic European scooters. Powering the NS150LA is a modern 150cc liquid-cooled, four-valve SH-EP engine equipped with Honda’s PGM-FI electronic fuel injection, a silent ACG starter, and Idling Stop, all contributing to responsive performance, smooth starts, and excellent fuel efficiency with an estimated range of over 350 km. Safety and convenience are well addressed, with dual-channel ABS and TCS (Traction Control System) offered as standard across the lineup. The higher-end “Pro” variants elevate the package further with a TFT smart display featuring smartphone connectivity, a Smart Key system, a factory-fitted front dashcam, and tire pressure monitoring, firmly positioning the NS150LA as a premium, tech-forward contender in the mid-sized scooter segment.

Honda has introduced the new Honda CG125 2027 lineup, continuing its popular 125cc commuter motorcycle range with three main variants: the CG125, CG125S, and CG125S Gold. The standard CG125 is available in Red, Black, and the newly introduced Silver color, while the CG125S comes in Red and Black and offers self-start convenience along with updated styling. The top-spec CG125S Gold is also offered in Red and Black, featuring distinctive gold-themed graphics and a more premium appearance. All variants retain the familiar 125cc 4-stroke OHV air-cooled engine, while the CG125S variants are equipped with a 5-speed transmission and self-start system. Overall, the 2027 models focus mainly on refreshed graphics, new color options, and styling updates while maintaining the reliability, familiar design, and everyday practicality that the CG125 lineup is known for.

The newly launched Triumph Tracker 400 2027 brings a raw, minimalist flat-track character to Triumph’s popular 400cc Modern Classic lineup. Built on the same platform as the Speed 400, the Tracker sets itself apart with a purpose-tuned chassis, including a slightly reduced wheelbase and a more upright, commanding riding stance created by wider handlebars and revised footpeg positioning. At its heart is an updated 398cc liquid-cooled, single-cylinder TR-Series engine, producing a modest increase in peak output to a claimed 41.4 hp. Styling highlights such as the sharp flyscreen, body-coloured rear cowl, and 17-inch cast aluminium wheels fitted with chunky Pirelli MT60 RS tyres—flat-track inspired yet optimised for road use—give the Tracker a distinctive presence. Combined with competitive pricing, renowned Triumph build quality, and modern features like switchable traction control and ABS, the Tracker 400 positions itself as an appealing, fun, and accessible choice for riders who want standout styling and an engaging on-road experience.

Description:
Honda has introduced the newly launched Honda CD70 Dream 2027, featuring a refreshed design aimed at young, style-conscious urban commuters. The latest model comes with updated dynamic graphics and new body decals across its classic color options, including Red, Black, and Blue, giving the motorcycle a sportier appearance while retaining its signature front cowl visor, aerodynamic bodywork, and comfortable contoured seat.
Beneath the updated styling, the Honda CD70 Dream 2027 continues to use its proven mechanical platform. It is powered by a reliable 72cc air-cooled, 4-stroke OHC engine paired with a 4-speed constant mesh transmission, a kick-start system, and an 8.6-liter fuel tank. Built for excellent fuel efficiency, low maintenance costs, and smooth everyday commuting, the 2027 model offers an ideal combination of modern styling, dependable performance, and practicality for budget-conscious riders.

The newly launched Lifan KPR 200 (4V) and KPR 250 mark a significant upgrade for the series, evolving from budget-friendly commuters into more serious entry-level sportbikes. Both models now feature aggressive, wind-tunnel-tested fairings, sharp LED lighting with signature DRLs, and a fully digital LCD instrument cluster that provides high-contrast visibility for night riding. The standout improvement is the move to a 4-valve, liquid-cooled EFI engine architecture, which significantly boosts performance: the KPR 200 now pushes roughly 20 HP, while the 250cc variant steps up to a more robust 27-28 HP.
Safety and handling have also seen a major overhaul, with the inclusion of dual-channel ABS as standard and a refined 6-speed transmission that offers a smoother, ride-by-wire feel. Despite their "race-ready" look, both bikes maintain an ergonomic balance that favors daily usability, featuring a seat height of approximately 770–790 mm and a slightly upright clip-on handlebar position. With their combination of modern tech, competitive fuel economy (averaging 30–40 km/L), and a lightweight chassis, these bikes are positioned as top contenders for riders looking for a premium sportbike experience without the high price tag of Japanese alternatives.

The Honda CD 70 2027 continues Honda's long-standing tradition of delivering outstanding fuel efficiency, everyday reliability, and low maintenance costs for daily commuters. Following the brand's signature update cycle, the 2027 model features refreshed body graphics and subtle cosmetic enhancements while retaining its proven chassis and time-tested mechanical setup. Powered by the familiar 72cc air-cooled, 4-stroke OHC engine paired with a 4-speed constant mesh transmission, the CD 70 maintains its lightweight construction, classic kick-start system, and strong resale value. For riders seeking an affordable and dependable commuter that can easily handle city traffic and rough roads with minimal maintenance, the Honda CD 70 2027 remains the benchmark in the 70cc commuter motorcycle segment.

The Lifan CUB-ADV (LF125-26R) is a unique "crossover" motorcycle that bridges the gap between a traditional city underbone (cub) and a rugged adventure bike. Designed to handle both paved streets and light off-road trails, it features a 119.7cc single-cylinder, air-cooled, four-stroke engine that delivers approximately 6.0 kW (8 HP) of power and 8.5 N·m of torque. Its standout "ADV" styling is underscored by spoke wheels, a front disc brake, and an elevated stance, giving it a more aggressive look than a standard scooter. With a lightweight frame of just 105 kg and a 4-speed auto-clutch transmission, the LF125-26R is built for maneuverability and ease of use. Modern touches like an LCD digital meter and LED lighting complement its utility, while its impressive fuel economy—rated at roughly 1.6L/100km—makes it a practical choice for riders seeking a versatile, dual-purpose commuter.

The Lifan Starship 6 (LF600-C) has recently debuted as the premium flagship of Lifan’s high-end PFMoto (Paifang) brand, positioning itself as a serious contender in the luxury touring segment with a design clearly inspired by the Honda Gold Wing. Often described as a “land yacht,” it is powered by a self-developed 573cc, V-twin, liquid-cooled engine that produces approximately 40 kW (54 hp) and 55 Nm of torque. The motorcycle makes a strong visual statement with its massive proportions, weighing 325 kg and featuring a long 1,616 mm wheelbase. It also boasts a technology-rich cockpit, including a multi-screen intelligent central console, an electrically adjustable windshield, and a six-channel audio system.
Complementing the flagship is its mid-range sibling, the Starship 4 (LF400-3), which acts as an accessible bridge between the entry-level Starship 3 and the top-tier Starship 6. While the Starship 4 retains much of the Starship 6’s distinctive design language and grand-touring ergonomics, it is powered by a smaller 397.5cc V-twin engine that delivers around 29 kW (39 hp).

The newly launched Benelli BKX 125 2026 is a striking entry-level adventure motorcycle designed specifically for the A1 license category, making its market debut in early 2026. Styled by the Benelli Style Center in Pesaro, Italy, it features a minimalist yet futuristic aesthetic, highlighted by a vertical LED headlight assembly and distinctive handguards with integrated indicators. Powering the bike is a new liquid-cooled 125cc single-cylinder engine producing 15 hp at 9,500 rpm and 12.1 Nm of torque, pushing the legal limits of its class for maximum performance. Built for versatility, the BKX 125 uses a steel trellis frame, fully adjustable 41 mm upside-down forks, and 180 mm of suspension travel, allowing it to transition seamlessly from city streets to light off-road trails. With a lightweight curb weight of 144 kg, a 12-liter fuel tank offering nearly 500 km of range, and a 19-inch front spoked wheel, the BKX 125 positions itself as a premium yet accessible gateway for the next generation of adventure riders.
specs: Single cylinder, 4 stroke, 4 valve, liquid cooled
41 mm upside-down forks full adjustable in spring preload and hydraulic brake rebound and compression
Rear swing arm in steel, shock absorber with progressive link, adjustable in spring preload and hydraulic brake rebound
Single floating disks 280 mm with 4 pistons calliper with and ABS
Single disc 240 mm with floating calliper single piston and ABS

Brembo Dual floating discs, 4-piston caliper with ABS

Segway Custom High?Performance Mid?Mounted Flat?Wire Motor
Marzocchi 37mm thickened fork, 220mm long travel(Full adjustable compression and rebound)
Marzocchi multi-link structure(Full adjustable compression, rebound and preload)
Front and rear 4-piston hydraulic disc with 220 mm X 3 mm rotors
2 years on major components (motor, battery, frame); 1 year on the full bike

Description: The SYM TTLBT 2026 is a high-performance maxi-scooter designed to bridge the gap between everyday commuting and long-distance sport touring. Launched as SYM’s flagship model for 2026, it is powered by a 508cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin engine producing approximately 45 hp and 49.9 Nm of torque, placing it in direct competition with class leaders such as the Yamaha TMAX. Its “Turtle” namesake references a Chinese symbol of longevity and tenacity—a theme reflected in its generous storage capacity, totaling 65 liters across a 37-liter under-seat compartment and integrated side panniers. Tech-forward and comfort-focused, the TTLBT features a 7-inch TFT display with Apple CarPlay, an electrically adjustable windshield, heated grips, and a sophisticated Bosch electronics suite, including IMU-controlled cornering ABS and traction control.

Launched in early January 2026, the Honda UC3 is a significant addition to Honda’s electric lineup, positioned as a 110cc-equivalent “Intelligent Urban Life Partner.” Departing from the brand’s recent focus on swappable batteries, the UC3 introduces Honda’s first fixed Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery, offering a more durable and cost-effective solution for daily commuters. It delivers a respectable claimed range of 122 km on a single charge and a top speed of 80 km/h, powered by a 6.0 kW wheel-side motor. The design is distinctly futuristic, characterized by flowing curves, a signature horizontal LED light bar, and a premium black-and-gold color scheme. Tech-forward features such as a 5-inch TFT display with Honda RoadSync, a smart key system, and reverse assist further enhance its appeal for navigating dense urban environments.
specs: 4 hours(from 30% to 80%), 9 hours (from 0% to 100%) for 450W charger

Description:
The newly launched Bajaj Chetak C2501 (also known as the Chetak C25 ) marks a strategic shift for the brand, positioning itself as its most affordable and accessible electric scooter to date. Designed specifically for urban agility, it sheds approximately 22 kg to achieve a nimble kerb weight of 107 kg. Unlike its more expensive siblings, the C25 is powered by a 2.2 kW hub-mounted motor paired with a 2.5 kWh NMC battery, delivering a practical top speed of 60 km/h and a claimed IDC range of 113 km.
Despite being positioned as an entry-level model, it retains the premium all-metal body and IP67 water resistance that define the Chetak legacy. The scooter also introduces several design updates, including a new horizontal LED tail-lamp and a more conventional telescopic front fork for improved handling on city roads. On the practicality front, it offers a 25-litre under-seat storage compartment and a colour LCD console with Bluetooth connectivity, making it a competitive, no-nonsense choice for daily commuters seeking durability and style without a premium price tag.

The NIU XQi 500 2026 is a high-performance electric enduro bike designed to bridge the gap between lightweight e-motos and full-sized dirt bikes. Moving beyond the urban focus of its predecessor, the XQi3, the XQi 500 delivers a substantial boost in performance with a 28.8 kW (approximately 39 hp) peak output and a high-voltage 96V 40Ah battery system. This setup allows for a highway-capable top speed of up to 75 mph and produces 100 Nm of instant torque, positioning it as a serious contender in the road-legal 125cc-equivalent category. Despite its impressive power, the bike remains agile thanks to its lightweight 92 kg (203 lb) chassis and is equipped with premium components such as dual-channel ABS, traction control, and fully adjustable KKE suspension.

Features: Drum Variant; Disc Variant; XTEC
Description:
The Hero Passion Plus has long been a staple of the commuter segment, celebrated for its “fill it, shut it, forget it” reliability and iconic slanting engine design. Originally launched to bridge the gap between utility and style, the Passion Plus has recently been revived with modern updates such as i3S technology (idle stop-start system) and integrated USB charging, while retaining its signature comfortable ergonomics and impressive fuel efficiency.
For riders seeking a bit more punch and contemporary features, the Passion Pro serves as the more modern sibling. The Passion Pro has evolved through several distinct variants to cater to different budget and performance needs:
Drum Variant: The base model, featuring dependable mechanical drum brakes at both ends.
Disc Variant: Equipped with a front disc brake for significantly improved stopping power and safety.
XTEC: The premium trim, introducing a fully digital instrument cluster, Bluetooth connectivity for call and SMS alerts, and a signature LED projector headlamp.
Whether you choose the nostalgic, rugged simplicity of the Passion Plus or the tech-forward XTEC variant of the Passion Pro, the Passion series remains a masterclass in delivering a premium feel within the 100–110cc commuter category.

The SYM Cruisym 400 2026 marks a significant evolution in the maxi-scooter segment, stepping up from its 300cc predecessor (Cruisym 300) to a more robust 399cc single-cylinder, liquid-cooled engine. This new powerplant produces a respectable 34 hp and approximately 27 lb-ft of torque, positioning it as a direct competitor to established rivals such as the Yamaha XMAX 400 and Honda Forza 350. Designed with a touring-oriented philosophy, the Cruisym 400 features sharp, aggressive bodywork, a three-position adjustable backrest for long-haul comfort, and full LED lighting for enhanced visibility. Its technology package is particularly impressive for the segment, highlighted by a 7-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity for turn-by-turn navigation and a unique integrated dash cam—a rare standard feature that caters to modern, safety-conscious commuters.
specs: 4 STROKE, SINGLE CYLINDER, OHC, LIQUID COOLED, 4-VALVE
Hydraulic Single Side Arm Front Suspension
Front: Disc Brake - 8.7" Rear: Disc Brake - 8.7"

Description: The newly released QJ Motor SRT 125 DX 2026 is an exciting entry in the 125 cc adventure motorcycle segment for 2026, designed to bridge the gap between urban commuting and light off-road exploration. Featuring a liquid-cooled, single-cylinder engine that delivers about 11 kW (15 hp) and 12.5 Nm of torque, it offers smooth and lively performance that’s well-suited for riders with an A1 or B licence – giving plenty of fun both on paved roads and gravel tracks. The bike boasts a typical adventure setup with 21″ front and 18″ rear spoked wheels, a high ground clearance of around 225 mm, and a comfortable upright ergonomics. Its chassis includes quality suspension with a front upside-down fork and a rear mono shock, while safety is enhanced with disc brakes and ABS. A modern TFT display, full LED lighting and practical features like elevated exhaust and mounting points for luggage make the SRT 125 DX both stylish and capable for daily rides and weekend escapes into light terrain.

The newly released Kymco Downtown GT 125i represents a significant evolution in the 125cc maxi-scooter category, blending "Grand Touring" comfort with modern urban agility. For 2026, the model features a liquid-cooled, 4-valve SOHC engine that delivers approximately 12.7 hp and 11 Nm of torque—a notable 13% increase in power over its global predecessor. Safety is a primary focus, as the GT 125i comes equipped with a comprehensive electronics suite including ABS, a Traction Control System (TCS), and an Emergency Stop Signal (ESS) that flashes the LED taillights during sudden braking.
The chassis has been refined with a 2.5% lighter frame and a move to larger 15-inch front and 14-inch rear wheels to improve high-speed stability and ride quality. Practicality remains a hallmark of the Downtown series, offering a spacious under-seat compartment capable of housing two full-face helmets, alongside modern tech like a 7-inch TFT dashboard, keyless ignition, and a USB charging port. With its sharp, "Tension in Motion" design language and a 12.5-liter fuel tank, the GT 125i is positioned as a premium, tech-forward choice for both daily commutes and weekend excursions.
specs: Single-Sided Swinging Fork with Adjustable Swing Preload

Description: The newly released QJ Motor SRK 421 RR (sometimes referred to as the SRK 450 RR in specific markets) has officially entered the ring to challenge the Kawasaki Ninja ZX-4RR for 400cc inline-four supremacy. This high-revving "screamer" features a 421cc, 16-valve DOHC engine that produces a claimed 76.4 hp (77.6 PS) at 14,000 rpm, virtually mirroring the performance of its Japanese rival while offering slightly more torque 39 Nm thanks to its extra displacement. Beyond the engine, the bike is a spec-sheet powerhouse, boasting premium hardware including fully adjustable Marzocchi suspension, Brembo radial brakes, and a comprehensive electronics suite featuring a 7-inch TFT display, cornering ABS, and a bi-directional quickshifter. Wrapped in "Mecha-inspired" aerodynamic bodywork with functional winglets and a hollowed tail section, the SRK 421 RR positions itself as a disruptive, high-value alternative that undercuts the competition's price tag without sacrificing track-ready components.
specs: Marzocchi upside-down (USD) telescopic forks, fully adjustable

Description: The newly launched CFMOTO ZForce Z10 (and its four-seat sibling, the Z10-4 ) represents a massive leap for the brand, firmly planting it in the high-performance sport Side-by-Side (SxS) category. At its heart is an all-new 998cc turbocharged triple-cylinder engine that pumps out a punchy 143 hp and 136 Nm of torque, making it a direct competitor to industry titans like the Polaris RZR XP and Can-Am Maverick X3. To handle that power, CFMOTO equipped it with their "OmniDrive" CVT and a sophisticated suspension system featuring 2.5-inch FOX QSE shocks, which allow riders to toggle between Soft, Medium, and Firm settings on the fly. Inside, the "futuristic" cabin is headlined by a massive 12.3-inch RideSync touchscreen with Apple CarPlay, a backup camera, and a supercar-inspired multi-function steering wheel.
specs: High clearance double A-arm independent, 431mm travel

Description:
The Bimota KB399 Espresso, officially unveiled on March 18, 2026, represents a refined, Italian-styled evolution of the high-revving Kawasaki Ninja ZX-4RR. Positioned as a "small but intense" addition to Bimota’s lineup, it utilizes the 399cc inline-four engine from its Kawasaki donor, delivering a claimed 80 hp (59 kW) at 14,500 rpm with ram-air induction. While it retains the core steel trellis frame of the ZX-4RR, the KB399 distinguishes itself with premium cycle parts and Bimota’s signature design language, including aerodynamic winglets integrated into the fairing and a custom titanium Akrapovic silencer as standard. The handling is significantly sharpened via an upgraded 41mm Showa SFF-BP front fork and Brembo Stylema radial calipers, replacing the more basic components found on the original Kawasaki platform.
For those seeking even more exclusivity, Bimota has also introduced the Edizione Speciale (ES) variant. This flagship version further reduces weight and enhances performance through dry carbon fiber bodywork, billet aluminum adjustable footpegs, and a high-spec Ohlins STX46 rear shock. Standard electronics across both models include a quickshifter, three-mode traction control, and integrated riding modes, all accessible through a 4.3-inch color TFT display. With its distinctive red, white, and black livery, the KB399 Espresso aims to provide the boutique Bimota experience in a more accessible mid-capacity package, bridging the gap between urban agility and track-focused precision.

The BMW M 1000 R 2026 is a cutting-edge hyper-naked motorcycle that blends superbike performance with aggressive roadster styling, making it one of the most extreme street-legal machines from BMW Motorrad. Powered by a 999cc inline-four engine derived from the brand’s race-focused RR models, it delivers around 205–210 horsepower, enabling blistering acceleration and a top speed close to 280 km/h. The bike features advanced electronics such as Dynamic Traction Control, multiple riding modes, launch control, and BMW’s quick-action throttle, ensuring precise control both on the road and track. Its lightweight aluminum frame, carbon fiber components, and aerodynamic winglets enhance handling and stability at high speeds, while premium hardware like electronically adjustable suspension and ABS Pro adds to its performance-focused package. With its bold design, aggressive LED lighting, and motorsport DNA, the M 1000 R 2026 stands as a perfect fusion of everyday usability and track-ready power for adrenaline-seeking riders.
specs: Water/oil-cooled in-line four-cylinder, four-stroke engine with four titanium valves per cylinder and BMW Shiftcam variable intake camshaft control
Constant-mesh 6-speed gearbox integrated in the transmission housing
Upside-down telescopic fork, diameter 45 mm, electronic self-adjusting DDC Dynamic Damping Control, spring preload, rebound and compression stages adjustable
Aluminum twin-sided swingarm, DDC Dynamic Damping Control (central shock absorber), adjustable spring preload, rebound and compression stages electronically adjustable
Twin disc brake, diameter 300 mm, 4-piston fixed caliper
Single disc brake, diameter 220 mm, 1-piston floating caliper
82.1" x 39.2" (above mirror) x 46.3" (above mirror, at unladen weight)
Eco / Comfort / Sports / Sports+ / Master / Wet

Description:
The 2026 Bajaj Pulsar 180 has made a significant comeback, bridging the gap between the Pulsar 150 and the 220F with a blend of heritage styling and modern functional updates. The new model retains its iconic muscular silhouette but now adopts a full LED lighting setup—including the headlamp and turn indicators—giving it a sharper, more contemporary road presence. Under the tank, it is powered by a refined 178.6cc single-cylinder, air-cooled engine that produces 17 PS and an improved 15 Nm of torque, now updated for E20 fuel compatibility and the latest emission standards.
The updated cockpit features a fully digital LCD instrument cluster with Bluetooth connectivity for call and SMS alerts, alongside a standard USB Type-A charging port for mobile devices. While the mechanical underpinnings remain robust—with 37mm telescopic front forks, twin gas-charged rear shocks, and a 280mm front disc brake with single-channel ABS—the ergonomics have shifted slightly toward comfort, thanks to a new single-piece seat replacing the previous split-seat design.
Available in premium color schemes like Black Gold, Black Blue, and Black Red, the 2026 Pulsar 180 positions itself as a practical yet sporty commuter for riders seeking reliable performance without the complexity of higher-displacement machines.
specs: 4 Stroke, Air cooled, Single Cylinder DTSi
Twin Shock absorber, Gas filled with Canister
Fully Digital Reverse Monochrome LCD Speedometer with Bluetooth connectivity
35/35 W with 2 pilot lamps, With AHO (Auto Headlamp On)

Description: The VinFast Viper 2027 electric scooter is a modern, sporty electric scooter designed to deliver a balance of performance, smart technology, and everyday practicality. Developed by VinFast, the Viper features a bold and aggressive design with sharp styling and LED lighting, giving it a premium urban appeal. It is powered by a 3,000W BLDC hub motor that enables a top speed of around 70 km/h, making it suitable for both city commuting and short highway runs. The scooter comes with a removable 1.5 kWh battery (with an option for an additional pack), offering a claimed range of up to 156 km, along with flexible charging options. It also incorporates smart features such as a TFT display, keyless start, vehicle tracking, and remote anti-theft functions, while dual rear shock absorbers and hydraulic suspension ensure a comfortable ride. Overall, the Viper stands out as a feature-rich electric scooter aimed at riders looking for a stylish, tech-savvy, and eco-friendly mobility solution.
specs: Approximately 82 km (+74 km with additional battery)
Approximately 4 hours and 30 minutes from 0 to 100%

Description: The KTM Freeride E 2027 is the latest evolution of KTM’s electric enduro lineup, designed to deliver lightweight performance, instant torque, and near-silent trail riding. Powered by a refined electric drivetrain producing up to 19.2 kW of peak power and around 37 Nm of torque, it offers strong low-end acceleration with a top speed of approximately 95 km/h. The bike features a new 5.5 kWh swappable lithium-ion battery that provides an estimated 2–3 hours of off-road riding, along with three selectable ride modes and adjustable energy recuperation settings for improved efficiency. Built on a lightweight chrome-molybdenum steel frame with WP XACT/XPLOR suspension, the Freeride E emphasizes agility and control, while its 112 kg weight and low center of gravity make it easy to handle on technical terrain. With low maintenance, minimal noise, and even road-legal capability in some markets, the 2027 model represents a significant step forward in practical and fun electric off-road motorcycling.
specs: WP XPLOR shock absorber with PDS
Liquid-cooled, interior permanent magnet synchronous motor
e-boost, Idling Stop Function, Regenerative System, TFT Color Instrumentation with Smartphone Connectivity via RIDEOLOGY THE APP

Single 220mm disc with single-piston caliper and ABS

Description:
The newly unveiled BMW F 450 R is a lightweight, dynamic streetfighter designed to target the global A2 license category. Positioned directly below its larger Roadster siblings, it draws sharp design cues from the flagship S 1000 R while introducing an all-new 420 cc parallel-twin engine. Producing 48 hp (35 kW) and 43 Nm of torque—with 80% of its torque available at just 3,000 rpm—the engine features a 135-degree crankpin offset, delivering strong low-end punch along with a distinctive twin-cylinder exhaust note. Weighing just 175 kg wet, the bike offers an impressive power-to-weight ratio designed to maximize street agility and urban maneuverability.
Beyond raw performance, the F 450 R comes equipped with premium electronics and chassis hardware typically reserved for higher-tier motorcycles. It features a 6.5-inch TFT color display with smartphone connectivity, three riding modes (Rain, Road, and Dynamic), standard heated grips, and a radial Brembo front brake system supported by BMW ABS Pro, Dynamic Traction Control, and Dynamic Brake Control. Additionally, BMW offers its new centrifugal Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) on select variants. The system operates automatically based on engine speed, allowing smooth gear changes without the need to pull the clutch lever, making urban commuting virtually stall-proof.

Electronic intake pipe injection / digital engine management system with throttle-by-wire

Description: The newly launched BMW F 450 RR 2027 brings authentic supersport DNA and track-inspired styling to the accessible A2 licence category. Taking sharp visual cues from the flagship S 1000 RR, it features aggressive winglets, a distinctive split-face front design, and a clean underbelly exhaust. The motorcycle is powered by a lively 420cc parallel-twin engine that produces 48 hp and 43 Nm of torque. Weighing just 177 kg ready to ride, its lightweight chassis features a 43mm KYB upside-down fork and Brembo braking hardware for sharp, confidence-inspiring handling. Blending everyday usability with advanced rider aids, including cornering ABS, dynamic traction control, a 6.5-inch TFT display, and an optional centrifugal Easy Ride Clutch, the F 450 RR offers an exciting, high-tech entry point into BMW's renowned performance lineup.
