Description: The QJ Motor COV 125 S 2026 arrives as a sharp, modern addition to the A1-license segment, specifically targeting younger riders or urban commuters looking for a blend of motard styling and practical performance. For the 2026 model year, it features a liquid-cooled, 125cc single-cylinder engine that pushes the category’s legal limit with roughly 15 hp and 12 Nm of torque, mated to a smooth 6-speed gearbox. Visually, the "S" model stands out with its supermoto DNA, featuring 17-inch wire-spoke wheels wrapped in road tires, an aggressive high-mounted front fender, and a sleek, one-piece seat designed for agility. The chassis is equally robust, utilizing an inverted telescopic fork and a petal-disc braking system with ABS to ensure stability on varying road surfaces. With a lightweight curb weight of around 129 kg and a compact 8-liter fuel tank, it offers an accessible and flickable riding experience that bridges the gap between a focused trail bike and a daily city runabout.
specs: MONOSHOCK with Lever with Preload Adjustment
320mm Disc with Dual Piston Caliper Ø25 + ABS
220mm Disc with Single Piston Caliper Ø30 + ABS

Description: The newly released Keeway RKR 350 (2026) is a race-inspired sportbike designed by Centro Stile Morbidelli in Italy, blending sharp, aerodynamic aesthetics with mid-range performance. At its core, it features a 321cc inline twin-cylinder, liquid-cooled engine that produces 38.9 hp at 9,500 rpm and 28 Nm of torque at 8,000 rpm, engineered to meet the latest Euro 5+ emissions standards. The chassis is built for precision, utilizing 40mm inverted front forks and an adjustable rear shock, paired with a robust braking system featuring a 320mm front disc, ABS, and a Traction Control System (TCS). Modern rider amenities include a 5-inch TFT digital dashboard with an integrated Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS), full LED lighting with projector lenses, and dual USB charging ports (Type-A and Type-C), making it a technologically competitive option for both urban commuting and spirited weekend rides.
specs: Daytime Running Light (DRL) + Led projector lenses for optimal visibility
MONOSHOCK with Lever with Preload Adjustment
320mm Disc with Dual Piston Caliper Ø25 + ABS
220mm Disc with Single Piston Caliper Ø30 + ABS

Description: The Yamaha Cygnus X 2026 marks a major evolution of Yamaha’s popular 125cc commuter, combining everyday practicality with surprisingly advanced technology. Fully redesigned for its seventh generation, the new model features a stiffer chassis, updated suspension, and refined CVT setup to deliver sharper, more responsive handling. It is powered by a 124cc Blue Core engine, tuned for improved acceleration and efficiency, while still maintaining the smooth, reliable performance the Cygnus lineup is known for. Notably, Yamaha has introduced traction control—a rare feature in this segment—enhancing safety on slippery roads. The scooter also gets aggressive new styling with LED lighting, a more premium finish, and modern touches like improved electronics and connectivity features. Overall, the 2026 Cygnus X stands out as a sporty yet practical urban scooter, designed to offer a higher level of refinement and technology in the lightweight commuter class.
specs: upgrade with a longer front fork

Description:
The Keeway V302C 2026 continues to establish its presence in the premium sub-300cc cruiser segment with the release of its 2026 Model Year (MY2026) update. This bobber-style motorcycle maintains its signature low-slung, muscular stance, characterized by a tear-drop fuel tank and minimalist bodywork. The most notable update for 2026 is the introduction of a striking new yellow color option, which joins the existing glossy red, grey, and black palette. Underneath its vintage-inspired aesthetic, the V302C is powered by a unique 298cc liquid-cooled V-twin engine delivering roughly 29 hp and 26.5 Nm of torque.
A standout feature remains its belt-drive system, a rarity in this displacement class that offers a quieter, smoother ride and reduced maintenance compared to traditional chains. The hardware is equally modern, featuring inverted (USD) front forks, adjustable dual rear shocks, and dual-channel ABS for the disc brakes. With a approachable seat height of 690 mm and a kerb weight of 175 kg, it is designed for accessibility without compromising on its "big bike" feel.

The newly released 2026 Yamaha Factor 150 (and its more premium DX variant) continues Yamaha's focus on efficient, future-ready urban mobility by blending rugged commuter practicality with modern styling cues borrowed from the FZ-S series. At its heart is the 149cc air-cooled, single-cylinder engine equipped with BlueFlex technology, allowing the bike to run on petrol, ethanol, or a mixture of both—offering a flexible and eco-friendly solution for daily riders. While both models feature a robust 15.4-liter fuel tank and a new digital blackout instrument cluster with an ECO indicator, the Factor DX steps up the sophistication with a redesigned LED headlight, an exclusive engine spoiler, and glossier body panels. Its lightweight 133kg frame and larger 18-inch wheels ensure agile handling through city traffic, making it a competitive choice for those seeking low maintenance costs without sacrificing a sporty, premium aesthetic.

The newly released Bajaj Avenger Street 220 signals a bold, urban-centric reintroduction for Bajaj’s cruiser lineup, stepping into the spot left vacant by the discontinued Street 160. Driven by the familiar 220cc air-oil-cooled DTS-i single-cylinder engine, it delivers a dependable 19.03 PS of power and 17.55 Nm of torque via a 5-speed gearbox. Striking a distinct contrast to its chrome-heavy "Cruise" sibling, the Street variant adopts a meaner, stealth-oriented look characterized by a fully blacked-out engine, exhaust system, and fork gaiters. It features practical 17-inch front and 15-inch rear alloy wheels wrapped in tubeless tires, a shorter smoked flyscreen, and lower, flatter handlebars that create an agile, command-oriented riding posture tailored for city traffic. Available in sleek Ebony Black and Cocktail Wine Red, it modernizes the rider interface with a full-LCD digital console featuring Bluetooth connectivity, a gear position indicator, and an integrated USB charging port, all while maintaining its highly accessible, signature low-slung 737 mm seat height.
specs: Single cylinder, Oil cooled, Twin Spark DTS-i, Fuel Injected, 4 stroke, SOHC, 2 valve
Telescopic with double anti friction bush

Description:
The QJ Motor SRV 300 (MY2026) has officially debuted, bringing a sharper and more refined “custom cruiser” appeal to the entry-level premium motorcycle segment. Retaining its core mechanical character, the bike continues to be powered by a 296cc liquid-cooled V-twin engine that delivers approximately 30 hp and 26 Nm of torque, offering a distinctive blend of smooth performance and cruiser-style personality.
For the 2026 model year, QJ Motor has focused on enhancing both styling and everyday usability. The updated SRV 300 now features a redesigned dual-exhaust setup that amplifies its muscular road presence, while a revised fully digital instrument cluster adds a more contemporary touch with integrated Bluetooth connectivity for improved rider convenience.
Visually, the motorcycle receives fresh graphics along with two new paint finishes—Glossy Red and Matte Black—helping the model stand out with a more premium and aggressive aesthetic. Despite the updates, the SRV 300 retains its approachable ergonomics, including a low 700 mm seat height and a manageable 164 kg kerb weight, making it especially appealing to newer riders and urban cruiser enthusiasts alike.
With its V-twin character, modern tech additions, and accessible riding dynamics, the MY2026 SRV 300 positions itself as a compelling alternative to the largely single-cylinder competition in the lightweight cruiser category.
specs: Spring Pre-load and Rebound / Compression Shock
USD fork, Ø 41 mm, fully adjustable
Mono shock, Steel swingarm, adjustable rebound and preload
Single floating disc ø300 mm with four-piston radial caliper and ABS
Single ø240 mm disc with single-piston floating caliper and ABS

Description: The newly released Suzuki Burgman 150 (marketed as the Burgman 15 in select overseas markets) marks a significant evolution for the lineup, stepping up from a maxi-styled commuter into a true, performance-oriented maxi-scooter. Built on a robust step-over underbone chassis, the scooter commands a muscular, premium road presence highlighted by an aggressive front apron, a split-LED headlight configuration with inverted horseshoe-shaped DRLs, and a tall aerodynamic windscreen. At its heart lies a more powerful 149cc single-cylinder engine that delivers 14.2 hp and 14.2 Nm of torque, pairing smooth acceleration with an efficient idle stop-start system. Beyond the power bump, Suzuki has heavily prioritized stability and rider confidence by equipping the scooter with larger 14-inch alloy wheels, a telescopic front fork, and dual rear shock absorbers. The tech and safety suite is equally upscale, introducing dual-channel ABS, a switchable traction control system, and a full-color TFT instrument display complete with smartphone connectivity and turn-by-turn navigation. Finished with premium conveniences like keyless ignition, an 18-watt USB Type-C charging port, and a generous 25-liter under-seat storage bay, the Burgman 150 positions itself as a highly capable, comfort-focused powerhouse for both urban grids and highway cruising.

The newly released Segway Myon commuter e-bike marks a major step forward into the high-tech “car-replacement” market, blending an elegant step-through aluminum-alloy frame with a massive suite of automotive-grade technology. It pairs a 500W hub motor, capable of delivering an impressive 85 Nm of torque, with a 722Wh UL-certified battery, offering a class-leading range of up to 80 miles per charge.
What truly sets the Myon apart is the Segway Intelligent Ride System, which features seamless electronic shifting via handlebar-mounted buttons, built-in turn signals, an integrated TFT navigation display, and a “TurboTuned” sensor algorithm that automatically detects hills and delivers extra torque precisely when needed. Designed to be highly theft-resistant, the bike is further enhanced with premium features such as Apple Find My tracking, proximity-based AirLock, a loud motion alarm, and optional add-ons like a rearview safety radar, making it an exceptionally smooth, secure, and futuristic option for tech-savvy urban commuters.
specs: Segway Hydraulic Disc Brake Front Two-piston, 180 mm Rotor
Segway Hydraulic Disc Brake Rear Two-piston, 180 mm Rotor

Description: The newly launched 2027 Kawasaki KX327 marks a major milestone for Kawasaki’s off-road lineup, introducing the brand’s first fuel-injected 327cc liquid-cooled two-stroke single-cylinder engine. Designed to blend the raw excitement of a traditional two-stroke with modern technology, the KX327 delivers strong low-end torque, crisp throttle response, and consistent performance across varying riding conditions thanks to its electronic fuel injection system. The motocross machine features a lightweight aluminum perimeter frame, KYB suspension components, factory-style brakes, electric start, selectable power modes, smartphone connectivity via RIDEOLOGY THE APP KX2, and aggressive KX-inspired bodywork. With its combination of lightweight handling, advanced electronics, and race-focused performance, the new KX327 is positioned as one of the most exciting motocross bikes to hit the market in years, bringing the legendary two-stroke experience into a new era.
specs: Inverted fork with adjustable compression and rebound damping
Uni-Trak, adjustable dual-range (high/low-speed) compression and adjustable rebound damping, and spring preload adjustability

Description: The newly released Segway Super Villain SX20T has officially arrived in the high-performance sport side-by-side (SSV) market, packing a massive mechanical upgrade over its predecessors. Breaking away from conventional CVT setups, the SX20T features an industry-first, car-derived 2.0L turbocharged inline 4-cylinder engine paired with a rapid-shifting 7-speed dual-clutch transmission (DCT) with steering-wheel-mounted paddle shifters. This potent combination unleashes a whopping 235 horsepower and 380 Nm of torque, allowing it to tackle extreme desert dunes and steep climbs with effortless acceleration. To handle that raw power, Segway outfitted the flagship utility terrain vehicle (UTV) with a premium K-Man 3.0 Damper System, which delivers a massive 20 inches of suspension travel up front and 21 inches at the rear, all riding on 15-inch aluminum beadlock wheels wrapped in rugged 32-inch off-road tires. Inside the cockpit, the tech-heavy machine feels more like a modern sports car than a traditional off-roader, boasting adjustable bucket seats with 6-point harnesses, a tilt-and-telescoping steering column, and a dominant 10.4-inch smart commanding touchscreen integrated with Segway's Smart Moving App for real-time vehicle diagnostics, over-the-air updates, and live trail navigation.
specs: 2.0T GDi 4-Stroke DOHC Inline Four Cylinder Turbocharged
7-Speed Automatic Transmission w/ Optional Manual Intelligent Paddle Shifting P/R/N/D
Dual A-Arm w/ Stabilizer Bar, 20” Wheel Travel
Multi-Link Trailing Arm w/ Stabilizer Bar, 21” Wheel Travel

Description:
The newly released Honda HooRide 125 (globally recognized as the HRD 125 ) is an aggressive, adventure-style crossover scooter developed under the Wuyang-Honda joint venture. Breaking away from traditional, conservative commuter designs, the HRD 125 embraces a rugged, "mechanical aesthetic" inspired by the iconic Africa Twin dual-sport motorcycle, complete with a sharp front beak, twin-pod LED headlights, C-shaped DRLs, and a two-position adjustable windscreen. Beneath its tough exterior beats the highly efficient 124.7cc liquid-cooled eSP+ engine borrowed from the PCX 125, pumping out 11 horsepower and 11.7 Nm of torque while delivering an impressive claimed fuel efficiency of up to 47.17 km/L.
What truly sets this mini-ADV scooter apart is its premium tech suite—features rarely seen in the 125cc segment—including a 5-inch TFT instrument cluster, dual-channel ABS, traction control, a tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS), and a dedicated handlebar mounting bar that can even sync up with DJI action cameras. Highly practical for daily grinds, it pairs a flat step-through floorboard with clever packaging; the 8.2-liter fuel tank is tucked inside the floor, freeing up enough underseat storage to fit two half-face helmets.

The newly launched Kawasaki KX327X 2027 marks a bold return to the big-bore two-stroke off-road segment, combining modern technology with the raw excitement that enthusiasts crave. Powered by Kawasaki’s all-new 327cc fuel-injected, liquid-cooled two-stroke single-cylinder engine, the KX327X delivers strong low-end torque, crisp throttle response, and improved efficiency across varying riding conditions. Designed specifically for cross-country and enduro-style riding, it features a wide-ratio 6-speed gearbox, electric start, lightweight aluminum perimeter frame, KYB suspension, Nissin brakes, and a larger fuel tank for extended adventures. The bike also benefits from smartphone connectivity via RIDEOLOGY THE APP KX2, selectable power modes, handguards, a skid plate, and other off-road-focused equipment. With its combination of lightweight agility, cutting-edge fuel injection technology, and race-ready performance, the KX327X 2027 is set to become one of the most exciting new off-road motorcycles in Kawasaki’s lineup.
specs: Inverted fork with adjustable compression and rebound damping
Uni-Trak, adjustable dual-range (high/low-speed) compression and adjustable rebound damping, and spring preload adjustability

Description:
Officially launched by Honda, the NS150XC is an adventure-style scooter heavily inspired by the ADV150 platform, delivering a rugged, modern, and highly capable package for both city commuting and light off-road exploration. Under the hood, it shares Honda's reliable 150cc liquid-cooled, four-valve eSP+ engine, which balances strong performance with excellent fuel efficiency, allowing for a riding range of over 350 kilometers on a full tank.
The NS150XC truly stands out with its premium chassis and comprehensive safety package. It comes equipped with KYB inverted front forks, a rear gas-charged suspension, and high-quality Nissin brake calipers. Raising the safety standards in the 150cc segment, it features dual-channel ABS, traction control (TCS), and an advanced Bosch cornering ABS system that enhances braking stability while cornering.
The technology package is equally impressive, featuring a TFT LCD instrument display, keyless ignition, Bluetooth smartphone connectivity via the T-Box system, and a built-in tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) for both the front and rear wheels. For touring enthusiasts, the upgraded Pro version further enhances practicality with factory-installed front and rear 1080p cameras, sturdy crash bars, hand guards, a two-stage adjustable windscreen, and a rugged rear luggage box.
specs: Hydraulic brake system (dual-channel ABS + cornering ABS, dual disc front & rear)

Description: The 2027 Beta 250 RXF (also designated as the RX 250 4T ) marks a historic milestone for the Italian manufacturer as its first-ever purpose-built 250cc four-stroke motocross bike, engineered completely from scratch. Stepping aggressively into the highly competitive MX2 class, the machine features an incredibly compact liquid-cooled, DOHC engine that weighs roughly 1.5 kg (3.3 lbs) less than the established class benchmark, utilizing thin-wall aluminum crankcases and lightweight magnesium covers to achieve superior mass centralization. Beta's engineers packed the power plant with a sophisticated dual-injector fuel injection system—placing one injector at the throttle body and a second at the airbox sleeve—to deliver crisp throttle response at low revs alongside an explosive high-end pull. The chassis features a model-specific, double-cradle chromoly steel frame with side-mounted head stays tuned for precision cornering, fully supported by premium, race-calibrated KYB 48mm closed-cartridge front forks and a matching KYB rear shock. Wrapped in a sharp, modern red-and-black livery that moves away from traditional white accents, this 2027 rookie comes fully race-ready with top-tier electronic rider aids including a five-level launch control system, two-level traction control, a quickshifter, and dual switchable engine maps.
specs: Single cylinder, 4 –stroke, liquid cooled, 4-valve (Titanium intake and exhaust), electric start
Molybdenum steel / Double Cradle w/ quick air filter access
48 mm KYB AOS closed cartridge fork, adjustable compression & rebound
KYB 50mm body with linkage, adjustable rebound, and high/low speed on compression adjustment

Description: The newly launched 2027 Ducati Desmo250 MX marks a thrilling new chapter in the Italian manufacturer's off-road racing expansion, delivering a high-tech machine tailored specifically for the competitive MX2 class. At its core sits a lightweight, 24.7 kg (54.4 lb) single-cylinder engine that leverages mechanical blueprints directly from the flagship Ducati Panigale V4 R, featuring the same 81 x 48.4 mm bore and stroke dimensions. Harnessing Ducati's signature desmodromic valve timing system—which replaces traditional valve springs with precise mechanical actuation—the 249.7cc powerplant produces a claimed 44.5 horsepower at 12,500 rpm and revs all the way to an industry-benchmark 15,000-rpm limiter, giving riders the strategic advantage of holding gears longer between corners. This potent engine is housed within a rigid twin-spar aluminum perimeter frame derived from its 450cc sibling, contributing to a remarkably nimble wet weight of just 227 pounds (excluding fuel). For maximum track precision, the bike is equipped with fully adjustable 49 mm Showa front forks and a rear monoshock featuring low-friction Kashima coatings. A comprehensive electronics package includes multi-level traction control, customizable engine maps, an upshift-only quickshifter, and a specialized Predictive Maintenance system managed via smartphone through Ducati's X-Link app.
specs: Desmo250, Liquid Cooled, 4 Stroke, 4 Valves, DOHC, Single Cylinder
Length x Width x Overall Height
Showa upside down front fork 49mm fully adjustable

Description: The newly launched Yadea Ova 2026 is an elegant, urban-focused electric scooter that combines a retro, vintage-inspired aesthetic with advanced electronic rider aids. Tailored specifically for daily city commuting, it features eye-catching, ballet-inspired styling, a distinctive 3D swallowtail rear design, and an ergonomic "cloud-soft" saddle optimized for comfort. Beneath its stylish exterior, the Ova is packed with premium safety technologies typically found on larger vehicles, including a Traction Control System (TCS) to prevent wheel slip on wet surfaces, Hill Descent Control (HDC), Hill Hold Control, and a convenient one-touch reverse function. Depending on the market variant, it is powered by a smooth wheel-hub motor producing up to 1,440 W of peak power, paired with an energy-efficient graphene battery that delivers a practical urban range of approximately 60 to 85 km (37 to 53 miles) and a top speed of around 40 km/h. Complementing its performance and safety credentials are modern smart features such as GPS tracking, Bluetooth app connectivity with keyless start functionality, and an electrically operated under-seat storage compartment. Altogether, the Yadea Ova positions itself as a safe, low-maintenance, and stylish solution for modern, eco-friendly urban transportation.

The newly released Yadea Osta series positions itself as a premium neo-retro urban electric scooter lineup that blends classic styling with advanced digital and mechanical technology. Manufactured at Yadea's high-tech production facility, the 2026 Osta range consists of four distinct variants—the H, H+, P, and an upcoming Battery Swap model —all unified by a chic dual-tone design featuring a premium leather seat, full LED lighting, keyless entry, and a robust IPX7-rated waterproof wheel-hub motor producing a peak output of 2,750 W (3.7 hp) and 20 Nm of torque. While visually identical on the road, each model's internal specifications are tailored to different commuting needs. The entry-level Osta H pairs a 72V 30Ah LFP battery with a standard digital display and a front disc/rear drum brake setup, delivering a WMTC-certified range of 70 km and a top speed of 63 km/h. The Osta H+ upgrades to an intelligent TFT display with smartphone mirroring and replaces the rear drum brake with a disc unit, while offering a 120 km range and a top speed limited to 49 km/h. At the top of the lineup, the flagship Osta P enhances practicality with a larger 72V 45Ah battery, extending riding range to an impressive 180 km while retaining a top speed of 63 km/h. Across all variants, riders benefit from a comprehensive suite of electronic rider aids, including a Traction Control System (TCS), Hill Hold Control (HHC), and Push Assist, making the Osta series one of the most technologically advanced and well-rounded urban commuter platforms currently available.

The Yadea COOLJOY is a smart, compact electric moped tailored specifically for effortless urban commuting and short-distance city travel. Built on a highly resilient frame that has endured rigorous load-vibration testing, it strikes a balance between lightweight agility and structural durability. The scooter features a 400W to 500W rear wheel hub motor—depending on the specific trim ( E, E3, or H )—delivering up to 58 to 75 Nm of responsive torque for smooth accelerations and effortless hill climbing.
Powering the vehicle is Yadea's signature TTFAR Graphene battery pack, available in 48V and 60V configurations, which delivers a reliable urban range of approximately 50 to 70 kilometers per charge, with a top speed electronically limited to around 25 km/h. Beyond core performance, the Cooljoy focuses heavily on modern rider utility, coming equipped with keyless Smart NFC unlocking, a vibrant, colorful HD digital display, high-brightness waterproof LED headlights, front hydraulic shock absorption, and practical additions like a front storage basket and an extended footplate.

The newly launched 2026 Yamaha RS Neo is a compact and highly agile 125cc scooter that leans heavily into sharp, streamlined "air force aesthetics." Tailored primarily for effortless urban commuting, it sets a class standard for accessibility with a remarkably light kerb weight of just 93 kg and a low 735mm seat height, making it incredibly nimble to handle in dense traffic. While its air-cooled engine puts out a modest 7.4 PS and 9 Nm of torque, it prioritizes real-world efficiency with an impressive claimed mileage of 57.9 kmpl. Coupled with practical touches like a front apron storage cubby, a USB Type-A charging port, a multifunction LCD console, and R1-inspired rear styling, the RS Neo delivers a balanced, no-frills commuter package that values lightweight maneuverability over sheer power.
specs: Air-cooled / Four-stroke / Single-cylinder / SOHC / 2V / Blue Core

Description: The newly launched Yadea GS70 2026 is an intelligent electric scooter designed specifically to meet the demands of modern urban commuting. Built around the manufacturer's "UR-ONE" sharp and aerodynamic design philosophy, it features a rugged frame with a 20% increase in stiffness and an impressive 18-layer anti-rust coating. On the performance front, it is powered by a rear-wheel hub motor paired with a robust 72V 30Ah LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) battery, delivering up to 2,800W of peak power and 105 Nm of maximum torque. This setup enables the scooter to reach top speeds ranging from 55 km/h to 75 km/h (depending on regional tuning) while providing a riding range of 81 to 100 kilometers on a single charge. Beyond its mechanical capabilities, the GS70 is equipped with premium rider-assistance features rarely found in its class, including a Traction Control System (TCS), Hill Descent Control (HDC), Cruise Control, and a 120-degree ultra-wide LED headlight with automatic darkness detection. The technology package is further enhanced by a smart TFT dashboard with integrated GPS navigation, app-based keyless entry, and a "Family Sharing" feature that allows up to five users to unlock and access the vehicle seamlessly.

The newly launched Honda Vario Evo 160 2026 builds on the sporty character of its predecessor while introducing meaningful updates that make everyday riding even more enjoyable. Its sharper, more aerodynamic bodywork is complemented by fresh color schemes, redesigned graphics, and premium touches such as 3D badging on the ABS variant, giving the scooter a more modern and refined appearance. Power comes from Honda's updated 157cc liquid-cooled, four-valve eSP+ single-cylinder engine, producing 15.4 PS and 14 Nm of torque. Revised engine tuning delivers stronger low- and mid-range acceleration while maintaining excellent fuel efficiency of around 46.7 km/l. Practicality has also been enhanced with the addition of a USB Type-C charging port, a pop-up center hook for carrying bags, an 18-liter under-seat storage compartment, full LED lighting, a digital LCD instrument cluster, Honda Smart Key keyless ignition, and an idling stop system. Depending on the variant, riders can choose between a Combined Braking System (CBS) or single-channel ABS, while 14-inch wheels, tubeless tires, and a lightweight chassis help the scooter feel stable yet nimble in city traffic. With its balanced blend of lively performance, modern technology, and everyday convenience, the Honda Vario Evo 160 remains one of the most well-rounded premium scooters for riders seeking both practicality and a sporty edge.
specs: Combi Brake System (CBS) & Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)
Single Cylinder, 4-Stroke, 4 Valves, Liquid Cooled, Engine

Description: Keeway has officially entered the premium electric scooter segment with the launch of the Hypevolt-R, its new high-performance flagship model. Powered by a robust mid-mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) delivering 12 kW (16 bhp) of peak power and 72 Nm of torque, the scooter accelerates from 0 to 40 km/h in just 2.3 seconds and reaches a top speed of 115 km/h. Power comes from a 5 kWh dual removable lithium-ion battery system, offering an impressive IDC-certified range of up to 180 km on a single charge. The battery can also be recharged from 0 to 80% in approximately three hours using the onboard charger. Beyond its impressive performance, the Hypevolt-R features a futuristic, sharp-edged design complemented by 14-inch alloy wheels. It also stands out with an extensive suite of advanced rider-assistance technologies, including dual-channel ABS, traction control, cruise control, hill-hold assist, blind-spot detection, and a dedicated rear-view camera integrated into a 5-inch TFT display, making it one of the most technologically advanced electric scooters in its segment.

The Yadea VEKOO 2026 is a highly efficient, technology-driven electric moped designed for effortless urban commuting and everyday student travel. Featuring a sharp, armor-inspired mecha-style front design and an upswept tail, it combines a compact, lightweight frame with an extra-large 350 × 300 mm footboard that provides generous legroom and additional storage space.
Powering the VEKOO is a quiet and smooth 400W continuous wheel-hub motor capable of delivering up to 1,000W of peak output, providing quick acceleration and a top speed of 38 km/h, making it ideal for city riding. To ensure a comfortable ride on uneven roads, it is equipped with dual hydraulic shock absorbers, durable 12-inch tires, and dependable drum brakes.
Depending on the variant (E, H, or P), the VEKOO is powered by a long-lasting 48V Graphene TTFAR battery that offers an estimated riding range of up to 65 km on a single charge.
What truly sets the Yadea VEKOO apart is its impressive suite of smart features. Through the Yadea App, riders can enjoy Bluetooth keyless unlocking, family account sharing for up to five users, a side-stand power safety cutoff, real-time GPS tracking, and customizable startup audio. These advanced technologies make the VEKOO one of the smartest and most cost-effective electric mopeds available for modern urban commuters.

The newly launched CFMoto CFLite 250 Dual is a nimble, entry-level enduro motorcycle designed to seamlessly bridge the gap between everyday urban commuting and weekend off-road adventures. As part of CFMoto's budget-friendly CFLite sub-brand, it moves beyond traditional air-cooled engines by featuring a modern 249cc liquid-cooled, SOHC, 4-valve, single-cylinder engine that delivers an impressive 24.5 hp and 22.5 Nm of torque, paired with a smooth 6-speed transmission. Weighing a manageable 154 kg (curb weight) and offering a generous 245 mm of ground clearance, the 250 Dual is well-equipped for challenging terrain with its 21-inch front and 18-inch rear spoked wheels, dual-channel ABS, full-LED lighting, and inverted front suspension.
Alongside it, CFMoto has also introduced the CFLite 230 Dual, a simpler and more rugged variant developed primarily for farm use and trail riding. Unlike its liquid-cooled sibling, the 230 Dual is powered by a durable, low-maintenance 229cc air-cooled single-cylinder engine with a traditional carburetor, producing 14.1 hp (10.5 kW) and 16.5 Nm of torque. It forgoes the complexity of ABS in favor of mechanical simplicity and reduces weight to just 132 kg (dry), making it an excellent choice for riders seeking a dependable workhorse rather than a feature-packed, street-legal enduro.

The CFMoto 250SR (Sport Racing) and its larger-displacement sibling, the 300SR (marketed as the 300SS in North America), stand out as highly competitive, entry-level supersport motorcycles that punch well above their weight class. Sharing a razor-sharp, aggressive design language inspired by the brand's larger race concepts, both models feature a rigid steel trellis frame, 37mm upside-down front forks, a central rear monoshock, and full LED lighting.
The primary distinction lies in their single-cylinder, liquid-cooled, DOHC powerplants. The 249cc engine in the 250SR generates approximately 27.5 hp and 22 Nm of torque, making it an agile, high-value option for quarter-liter markets. Meanwhile, the up-sized 298cc unit in the 300SR steps things up to 29.9 hp and 27 Nm of torque, delivering a broader midrange punch and an eager, high-revving top end. Both variants come equipped with a smooth 6-speed transmission paired with a slipper clutch to mitigate rear-wheel hop during aggressive downshifts. On the tech front, they boast a premium 5-inch TFT color display complete with Bluetooth connectivity, navigation features, and dual-channel Continental ABS squeezing radial-mounted calipers. With an approachable 780mm seat height and a lightweight curb mass hovering around 155 to 165 kg, the SR platform seamlessly bridges the gap between a forgiving commuter and a highly capable weekend track toy.

The CFMoto 1250TR-G 2026 has made a strong impact as the brand's flagship luxury grand tourer, representing a major leap forward for open-class touring motorcycles from China. Positioned to compete with premium rivals like the BMW R 1250 RT, this impressive machine is powered by a KTM-derived 1,279 cc liquid-cooled V-twin engine. Producing a robust 140 hp and 120 Nm of torque, it delivers effortless highway cruising while featuring premium components such as Brembo radial brakes and Marzocchi adjustable suspension.
CFMoto has equipped the 1250TR-G with an impressive range of advanced technologies, including a large 12.3-inch TFT color display—one of the biggest in the industry—built-in JBL surround sound speakers, an electronically adjustable windscreen, heated grips and seats, and a comprehensive suite of electronic rider aids. These include cornering ABS, cruise control, and a tire pressure monitoring system, making the 1250TR-G a highly capable and luxurious touring motorcycle.
specs: Ø48mm Upside down, Hydraulically adjustable, Marzocchi

Description: The Honda XR 300L 2026 (alongside its Tornado and Rally variants in regional markets) is a purpose-built, lightweight dual-sport motorcycle designed to bridge the gap between urban commuting and aggressive off-road riding. Built on a dual-cradle frame with long-travel suspension, featuring a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear spoked wheel setup, the bike offers impressive ground clearance and excellent terrain capability. It features rugged, minimalist bodywork, a sleek high-mounted exhaust, high fenders, and an upright, commanding riding position tailored for both seated and standing riding. Depending on the market, it is powered by a punchy single-cylinder engine tuned for strong low-end torque, such as the 293.5cc oil-cooled unit paired with a 6-speed gearbox, delivering smooth and responsive performance whether navigating city streets or tackling dirt trails. Standard features such as a high-visibility LCD instrument display, switchable dual-channel ABS, and powerful disc brakes ensure the 2026 Honda XR 300L remains a practical, accessible, and exciting motorcycle for dual-sport enthusiasts.
specs: Showa conventional telescopic fork with 221 mm of travel

Description: The Yadea Vora 2026 is a sleek, modern electric scooter designed to provide an efficient, technology-driven solution for daily urban commuting. Engineered as a compact, zero-emission vehicle, it combines a sharp, aerodynamic design with a comfortable riding position suitable for both students and working professionals. Beyond its stylish appearance, the Vora emphasizes practicality, featuring a long-lasting battery capable of delivering an impressive single-charge range, strong instant electric torque for effortless stop-and-go city riding, and responsive disc brakes for enhanced safety. It also comes equipped with a fully digital instrument cluster and modern smart connectivity features, including keyless access and an energy recovery system. With its combination of efficiency, convenience, and low maintenance, the Yadea Vora stands out as a compelling alternative to traditional gasoline-powered scooters in the rapidly growing eco-friendly mobility market.
specs: 72V 50Ah Battery: 188 km range 72V 30Ah Auxiliary Battery: Approximately 108 km range
72V 50Ah Battery: Approximately 137 km range 72V 30Ah Auxiliary Battery: Approximately 80 km range

Description:
The 2026 Harley-Davidson Deadwood is a factory-built, post-World War II-inspired bobber that strips the brands traditional Softail formula down to its rawest essentials. Built on the Softail chassis as a lowered, blacked-out counterpart to the Heritage Classic, the Deadwood captures the spirit of vintage garage-built custom motorcycles with chopped fenders, a solo tuck-and-roll seat, wire-spoke tubeless wheels, a short smoked windshield, and a single Denim Black paint finish.
Power comes from the air/oil-cooled Milwaukee-Eight 117 Classic V-Twin engine (1,923 cc), producing 98 hp and 120 lb-ft of torque. Paired with a 6-speed transmission and a 2-into-1 exhaust system, the engine delivers strong, effortless performance. Despite its minimalist, slammed silhouette, featuring a low 25.5-inch laden seat height and a hidden rear monoshock, the Deadwood is equipped with a comprehensive suite of modern technology. Standard features include a 6-axis IMU, Cornering ABS, lean-sensitive traction control, drag-torque slip control, three ride modes (Road, Sport, and Rain), full LED lighting, a Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS), and USB-C charging.
specs: Dual-bending valve 49 mm telescopic with aluminum fork triple clamps; dual rate spring; "beer can" covers
Hidden, free piston, coil-over monoshock; 43mm stroke; cam-style preload adjustment
Black Tubeless Laced w/ 36 Bright Spokes

Description:
The Honda CB500 Retro 2027 is a newly introduced retro-style roadster that takes a very different approach from Honda’s existing international 500cc motorcycles, such as the CB500 Hornet. Unveiled in 2026, the CB500 uses a 501cc air-cooled, single-cylinder engine rather than the 471cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin found in the international CB500 Hornet and CBR500R. The engine produces around 27.6 bhp and 43.3 Nm of torque and is paired with a 5-speed gearbox, giving the motorcycle a relaxed, torque-focused character suited to everyday riding and longer road trips. Honda has also equipped it with a slipper clutch and selectable torque control, while braking is handled by disc brakes at both ends with dual-channel ABS.
Visually, the Honda CB500 Retro follows a classic roadster formula, combining a relatively simple silhouette with modern equipment. Its styling is aimed at riders who want the presence of a large-capacity motorcycle without the aggressive appearance of a modern streetfighter. The bike is offered in three variants: the CB500 Alloy, CB500 Spoke Tubeless, and CB500 Spoke Tubeless with Stripe, with the main differences being the wheel design and additional graphics. The spoke-wheel versions use cross-spoke tubeless wheels, adding to the motorcycle’s traditional appearance while retaining the convenience of tubeless tyres. Honda offers the CB500 in four colours: Pearl Deep Ground Grey, Pearl Igneous Black, Matte Steel Silver Metallic, and Rebel Red Metallic. The Stripe version, meanwhile, gets its own Igneous Black finish with golden graphics.
The equipment list also gives the Honda CB500 Retro a modern touch. It features full-LED lighting, an analogue-digital instrument cluster, and Honda RoadSync smartphone connectivity, allowing riders to access connected functions through the motorcycle and a compatible smartphone. The selectable torque-control system adds another layer of electronic assistance, while dual-channel ABS provides additional braking control. Rather than chasing outright horsepower, the CB500’s character is centred on its larger single-cylinder engine, substantial torque, and classic styling. Honda’s decision to use a 501cc air-cooled single makes this model particularly distinct from the company’s internationally sold 471cc twin-cylinder CB500 models. For reference, the 2026 CB500 Hornet sold in other markets produces 47 hp and 43 Nm from its 471cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin engine, so the CB500 Retro should not be confused with that motorcycle despite the similar CB500 name.

The QJMotor SQ 350 2026 is a modern high-wheel urban scooter designed to bridge the gap between nimble city commuting and effortless highway cruising. Powered by a liquid-cooled, 330 cc single-cylinder SOHC engine producing around 30 horsepower and 33.5 Nm of torque, it delivers strong acceleration paired with a smooth automatic CVT transmission. Its standout chassis feature is the 16-inch alloy wheel setup, which provides excellent high-speed stability and absorbs uneven pavement far better than traditional small-wheeled scooters. On the safety and technology front, the SQ 350 comes well-equipped with dual-channel ABS, traction control (TCS), a 5-inch TFT color display with smartphone connectivity, keyless ignition, tire pressure monitoring, and even a built-in dashcam. Combined with a flat floorboard for a comfortable riding position and optional integrated top-case storage, it stands as a feature-packed contender aimed directly at mid-capacity urban commuters such as the Honda SH350i.
specs: 256 mm Disc With Dual Piston Caliper Ø27

Description:
Bajaj Auto has launched the Pulsar N160 S and the higher-spec Pulsar N160 SS side by side, introducing a heavily upgraded platform to the 160cc streetfighter segment. Both models share an all-new 164.5cc, 4-valve, oil-cooled engine producing 18.5 PS and 14.4 Nm of torque. The engine is paired with an Electronic Throttle Body (ETB), enabling four distinct riding modes—Road, Rain, Sport, and Off-Road—as well as low-speed Crawl Technology. Both models also feature the same hardware upgrades, including 37 mm gold-finished upside-down (USD) front forks, a rear monoshock, and a 300 mm front disc brake.
Where the two models differ is in their technology and safety features:
Pulsar N160 S: The standard upgraded variant comes with single-channel ABS and a 5-inch digital LCD instrument cluster with Bluetooth connectivity and turn-by-turn navigation.
Pulsar N160 SS: The flagship variant adds dual-channel ABS, a traction control system, adjustable clutch and brake levers, and a 5-inch color TFT display with full Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity. It also introduces segment-first Google Maps mirroring.
specs: Gear indicator, Clock, Fuel economy and Range indicator
Bi functional LED projector headlamp with LED DRLs

Description: The newly released Royal Enfield Himalayan 440 2027 brings back the raw, uncomplicated adventure spirit of the original Himalayan 411 while introducing key mechanical and usability upgrades. Celebrating ten years of the Himalayan nameplate, the motorcycle is powered by an upgraded 443cc, air-cooled, single-cylinder, long-stroke engine that produces 25.4 bhp at 6,250 rpm and 34 Nm of torque at 4,000 rpm. Crucially, it is now paired with a 6-speed gearbox, addressing the previous model’s limitations during highway cruising. Designed as a rugged yet highly accessible adventure motorcycle, it retains essential off-road features such as a 21-inch front wheel, 220 mm of ground clearance, and long-travel suspension, while lowering the seat height to an approachable 800 mm. Modern touches, including a round LED headlight, digital-analogue instrument cluster, Tripper navigation pod, switchable rear ABS, and Type-C charging, complete the practical touring package. The Himalayan 440 sits as a simpler and more affordable sibling below the liquid-cooled Himalayan 450.
specs: Single cylinder, 4-stroke, SOHC, air-cooled, fuel injection

Description:
The Ather Konarc 2027 is an electric scooter built on Ather’s new budget-focused EL-01 platform, marking the brand’s shift toward high-volume, family-oriented commuting. Designed with a sturdy steel unibody chassis and metal body panels for enhanced durability, the Konarc moves away from the aggressive, sharp styling of the 450 series in favor of a more mature design. It features a wide handlebar-mounted LED headlight, an apron-mounted U-shaped DRL, a long cushioned seat, and a spacious floorboard.
Available in two distinct trims, S-Line and Z-Line, the scooter comes with battery pack options ranging from 2.1 kWh to 3.5 kWh, delivering claimed IDC ranges of 100 km to 200 km and top speeds of up to 80 km/h. Practicality is a major highlight, with features such as 31-liter underseat storage, 14-inch front alloy wheels, telescopic front suspension, and a 450W onboard charger that makes convenient home charging possible.
The Ather Konarc is also equipped with modern technology, including a 7-inch DeepView display, Google Maps navigation, AutoHold, and the new Advanced Electronic Braking System (AEBS). Overall, the Ather Konarc strikes a balance between practicality, durability, and modern smart features, making it a promising option for family-oriented urban commuting.

The newly released Lambretta J200 2026 pays homage to the iconic 1960s J-Series while seamlessly incorporating modern engineering for urban commuters. Underneath its classic monocoque bodywork and long, low retro silhouette, the scooter is powered by a 174.5 cc liquid-cooled, single-cylinder engine that produces roughly 16.8 hp and 15.5 Nm of torque. Designed for agile city riding, it comes packed with contemporary features, including full-LED lighting with a signature headlight, a digital TFT display with smartphone connectivity, keyless ignition, and dual-channel ABS paired with front and rear disc brakes. Lambretta’s distinctive Double Arm-Link front suspension and twin rear shocks provide extra stability over rough pavement, making the J200 a refined blend of mid-century Italian style and modern everyday practicality.

Description: The newly released Yadea GT80 2026 stands out as a high-performance, premium electric cruiser engineered specifically for long-distance urban commuting and modern mobility. Powered by a wheel-hub motor delivering a peak output of 5,000 W, the GT80 reaches a top speed of up to 80 km/h and can easily handle inclines of up to 20-degree. Its core strength lies in its energy system, utilizing a 72V LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) battery with a standard 50 Ah unit paired with an optional 30 Ah expansion, providing an impressive total riding range of up to 170 km on a single charge. Safety and rider assistance are heavily prioritized, with features including Traction Control (TCS), Hill Descent Control (HDC), dual disc brakes with CBS, and a 40,000-CD high-output headlight. Complementing its commanding, shield-like aesthetic, the GT80 features a full-color TFT dashboard with smart connectivity, offering GPS tracking, geofencing, keyless app unlocking, and real-time battery management.
specs: 72 V 80 Ah (72 V 50 Ah standard + 30 Ah optional)
170 km (110 km standard + 60 km with optional battery)

Description:
The newly launched 2027 Can-Am Defender HD10 and HD11 bring a more powerful and capable platform to Can-Am’s utility side-by-side lineup. Designed for farming, ranch work, hunting, trail riding, mud, and heavy-duty hauling, the Defender range offers multiple configurations to suit different types of users. The HD10 is powered by Can-Am’s 80-hp triple-cylinder engine, while the HD11 steps things up with a new 999cc Rotax ACE triple-cylinder engine producing 95 hp and 70 lb-ft of torque. Both models use a CVT transmission and feature a rugged chassis, long-travel suspension, high ground clearance, and practical cargo solutions. Depending on the configuration, buyers can choose two- or three-person seating, while extended MAX versions provide seating for up to six people.
Can-Am Defender HD10 Models
The HD10 lineup includes the Can-Am Defender PRO DPS HD10, Can-Am Defender 6x6 DPS HD10, and Can-Am Defender DPS CAB HD10. Each version is designed around a specific type of utility work.
The Defender PRO DPS HD10 is built for demanding jobs, with an extended cargo box that provides plenty of space for tools, equipment, and other gear. The Defender 6x6 DPS HD10 adds a third driven axle, giving it extra traction and improving its ability to handle difficult terrain and heavy loads.
For users who need more protection from the elements, the Defender DPS CAB HD10 features a fully enclosed cab with HVAC, a hard roof, lined interior, full doors with electric windows and locks, and a windshield equipped with a wiper and washer system. This makes it a particularly practical choice for year-round work in rain, cold weather, dust, and other harsh conditions.
Can-Am Defender HD11
The more powerful Can-Am Defender HD11 is available in several configurations, including the Defender XU HD11, Defender XT HD11, Defender X mr HD11 with half-doors, and Defender Limited HD11.
The XU HD11 focuses on straightforward utility work, while the XT HD11 adds equipment aimed at more demanding trail use. Its standard features include a 4,500-lb winch, full hard roof, heavy-duty skid plate, front bumper, mudguards, and 29-inch XPS Trail King 2 tires.
At the top of the range, the Defender Limited HD11 combines the performance of the HD11 platform with a more premium cabin. It comes equipped with HVAC, full color-matched doors with power windows, a tinted rear window, Smart-Lok front differential, a 10.25-inch touchscreen, rear camera, and JL Audio sound system. The result is a more comfortable and refined side-by-side for users who want both utility and premium features.
Can-Am Defender X mr HD11 for Mud Riding
For riders who regularly tackle deep mud and challenging trails, the Can-Am Defender X mr HD11 with half-doors is one of the most specialized models in the lineup. It combines the 95-hp HD11 engine with Smart-Lok front differential technology, 30-inch XPS Swamp King tires, 14-inch aluminum wheels, a relocated 4,500-lb winch, steel rock sliders, wide mudguards, and full underbody protection.
Its premium half-doors offer a practical compromise between a completely open side-by-side and a fully enclosed cab. They help reduce the amount of mud, water, and debris entering the cabin while keeping the upper section open for improved visibility, airflow, and interaction with the surrounding environment.
Can-Am Defender MAX HD11 Six-Seat Models
The six-seat Can-Am Defender MAX models extend the same utility-focused formula to customers who need additional passenger capacity. The lineup includes the Defender MAX XT HD11, Defender MAX Limited HD11, and Defender MAX Lone Star CAB HD11.
The MAX XT HD11 provides seating for six people along with a 4,500-lb winch, 29-inch XPS Trail King 2 tires, hard roof, skid plate, heavy-duty bumper, and mudguards. The MAX Limited HD11 adds a higher level of comfort and technology, while the MAX Lone Star CAB HD11 is designed for buyers who prefer a more upscale enclosed-cab experience.
Defender MAX X mr HD11
Can-Am also offers the Defender MAX X mr HD11 with half-doors for customers who want six-seat practicality without sacrificing serious mud-running capability. Like the two- and three-seat X mr models, it uses the 95-hp HD11 engine, Smart-Lok front differential, 30-inch XPS Swamp King tires, aluminum wheels, relocated 4,500-lb winch, heavy-duty skid protection, steel rock sliders, and wide mudguards.
The half-door design is especially useful on the six-seat model because it gives passengers additional protection from mud and trail debris while maintaining the open-air feel that makes side-by-sides so appealing.
2027 Can-Am Defender Performance and Features
Across the range, the 2027 Can-Am Defender platform benefits from a redesigned chassis and suspension setup. HD11 models feature arched double A-arms and around 12 inches of suspension travel, helping the side-by-side remain composed over rough and uneven terrain.
The HD11 powertrain produces 95 hp and 70 lb-ft of torque from its 999cc liquid-cooled triple-cylinder engine. Depending on the model, buyers can also get features such as Smart-Lok or Quick-4Lok front differential technology, multiple drive modes, engine braking, and electronic belt protection.
With work-focused HD10 models, more powerful HD11 variants, premium Limited versions, mud-ready X mr configurations, and spacious six-seat MAX models, the 2027 Can-Am Defender lineup offers a wide range of choices. Rather than relying on a single configuration, Can-Am has developed different Defender models for everything from everyday farm work and hauling to serious trail riding, deep mud, and all-weather utility use.

Description:
The Yadea GT70 Cyber 2026 is a premium, adventure-inspired electric scooter designed to bridge the gap between basic urban commuters and long-range mobility vehicles. Powered by a robust 2,000W electric motor with a peak output of 3,200W, it can reach a top speed of up to 65 km/h, making it capable of keeping up with regular city traffic. Under its sharp, futuristic fairings, the scooter features long-lasting 72V Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) battery technology, with a standard 50Ah battery offering around 3.6 kWh of capacity and a claimed range of over 110 km on a single charge. For riders who need even more range, an optional dual-battery setup increases the total capacity to nearly 5.8 kWh, allowing for up to 170 km of range.
The GT70 Cyber also comes equipped with dual disc brakes, 12-inch wheels, 150 mm of ground clearance, a digital TFT display with turn-by-turn navigation, and regenerative braking. With its combination of practical range, modern technology, rugged styling, and useful features, the GT70 Cyber positions itself as a capable and versatile electric scooter for both everyday urban riding and longer journeys.

The newly launched Suzuki V-STROM 160 2027 brings Suzuki’s iconic Master of Adventure styling to an accessible, entry-level package. Powered by a fuel-injected, air-cooled 162cc SOHC engine paired with a 5-speed transmission, it produces 14.75 bhp and 14 Nm of torque, offering a balanced combination of everyday commuting efficiency and relaxed long-distance touring. The motorcycle features a distinctive octagonal LED headlight, a digital instrument panel, a USB charging port, and dual-channel ABS for enhanced safety. Designed for rider comfort and practical street touring, the V-STROM 160 combines an upright riding position and a low 795 mm seat height with dual-purpose tires, a 13-liter fuel tank, and a lightweight 148 kg curb weight. These features make it an approachable and stylish mini-ADV, well suited to both urban streets and weekend getaways.

The newly released Suzuki GN160 2027 is a neo-retro motorcycle that blends vintage commuter styling with modern performance and everyday practicality. Powered by an air-cooled, fuel-injected 162cc single-cylinder SOHC engine producing approximately 14 horsepower and 14.5 Nm of torque, paired with a 5-speed manual transmission, the bike is designed to be an agile and reliable urban commuter with light-cruiser appeal. It updates the classic Suzuki GN legacy with contemporary hardware, including single-channel front ABS, lightweight 18-inch aluminum alloy wheels, front fork rubber boots, dual adjustable rear shock absorbers, LED lighting, and a semi-digital round instrument cluster. With an approachable 770 mm seat height, an 11-liter fuel tank, a lightweight 128 kg curb weight, and 178 mm of ground clearance, the GN 160 offers accessible and comfortable ergonomics tailored for daily city riding and casual weekend outings.
specs: Swing-arm, Oil Damp with Adjustable Twin Shock

Description: The newly released Moto Guzzi Stelvio 2027 is a premium adventure motorcycle designed for riders who want long-distance touring capability without giving up the character of a traditional Italian bike. It is powered by Moto Guzzi’s 1,042cc liquid-cooled V-twin engine, producing around 115 hp, with shaft drive sending power to the rear wheel. The Stelvio features a 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheel setup, long-travel suspension, Brembo braking hardware, and a comfortable riding position suited to both highways and winding roads. Depending on the version, riders can also get modern features such as cornering ABS, traction control, riding modes, cruise control, a 5-inch TFT display, and smartphone connectivity. The Stelvio is available in standard and Stelvio PFF Rider Assistance versions, with the latter adding Moto Guzzi’s advanced radar-based rider assistance system. With its distinctive styling, shaft-driven V-twin character, touring-friendly ergonomics, and capable chassis, the Moto Guzzi Stelvio is aimed at riders looking for a versatile adventure bike with a distinctly Italian feel.
specs: Transversal 90-degree V-Twin, four valves per cylinder, liquid cooled with Ride by Wire

Features: Yamaha Crosser 150 Z ABS; Yamaha Crosser 150 S ABS
Description:
The 2027 Yamaha Crosser 150 is an entry-level dual-sport motorcycle designed to handle both daily urban commuting and light off-road adventures. It is powered by a 149cc air-cooled, flex-fuel single-cylinder engine that produces approximately 11.4 hp on gasoline and 11.7 hp on ethanol fuel, paired with a 5-speed transmission. The motorcycle combines practical commuter performance with adventure-focused equipment, including 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wire-spoked wheels fitted with Metzeler Tourance dual-purpose tires. It also features long-travel telescopic front forks, a rear Monocross suspension system, and single-channel ABS for improved control and braking confidence.
The Yamaha Crosser 150 2027 also comes with several modern features that improve everyday usability. These include full LED lighting, an updated digital instrument cluster with Bluetooth connectivity through the Yamaha Motor On app, a side-stand engine cut-off switch for added safety, and an integrated USB power outlet for charging compatible devices. With its upright riding position, rugged styling, and versatile suspension setup, the Crosser 150 is designed to offer a balance of comfort, practicality, and light off-road capability.
Available Models and Variants
Yamaha Crosser 150 Z ABS: The more off-road-focused version of the Crosser 150, featuring a high-mounted front adventure beak, protective front fork gaiters, and bold rally-inspired color schemes. Its styling and equipment give it a more rugged adventure appearance.
Yamaha Crosser 150 S ABS: The more urban-oriented version, featuring a lower, street-style front mudguard instead of the high-mounted adventure beak. It retains the same core chassis, engine, suspension, and mechanical components as the Z ABS variant, making it equally suitable for everyday riding and occasional light off-road use.
specs: Monocross type rear swingarm with linkage

Description: Unveiled in September 2026, the Aston Martin AMB 002 Roadster marks a historic milestone as the first road-legal motorcycle created through a partnership between Aston Martin and Brough Superior. Following the track-only AMB 001 and AMB 001 Pro, the AMB 002 translates Aston Martin’s hypercar design language into a street-ready machine, featuring sculpted carbon-fiber bodywork, signature side strakes, and tail-light blades inspired by the Valkyrie and Valhalla. At its core is a solid-billet titanium frame weighing just 5 kg (11 lbs), paired with an all-new CNC-machined 1,083cc water-cooled V-twin engine that produces 130 hp and 110 Nm of torque. Tipping the scales at just 190 kg (419 lbs), the roadster features a 50:50 weight distribution and a Fior anti-dive front suspension system, promising razor-sharp handling while maintaining everyday rideability. Hand-assembled at Brough Superior’s facilities in Toulouse, production of the AMB 002 is strictly limited to 300 units worldwide, with initial deliveries scheduled to begin in Q3 2027.

230 mm stainless steel disc with two-piston caliper

Description: The Gogoro Ezzy 500 2026 is a practical electric smart scooter designed specifically for urban commuters who need more power and range. Positioned above the entry-level Ezzy model, the Ezzy 500 features an upgraded 5.5 kW electric motor producing 7.4 hp and 133 Nm of torque, a dual-battery swapping system, and an extended range of up to 150 km. Designed with accessibility and value for money in mind, it features a low 745 mm seat height, a textured non-slip seat, and a spacious 28-inch flat footboard capable of carrying a full-sized suitcase. Modern convenience and automotive-level safety features include Slope Parking Assist (Auto Hold), Cruise Control, a Synchronous Braking System (SBS) with front and rear 180 mm disc brakes, four riding modes (Smart, Standard, Racing, and Low Battery), and an iOS- and Android-compatible LCD display.
specs: Negative display backlit color outer ring LCD

Description: Unveiled in October 2026, the newly introduced Aprilia SXR GT 125 updates Aprilia’s maxi-style scooter lineup with enhanced touring capabilities and fresh styling. Powered by a 124.45 cc single-cylinder engine producing 10 bhp and 10.4 Nm of torque, the SXR GT 125 combines a sporty stance with segment-first 14-inch wheels for improved stability on longer rides. Standard features include a signature Tripod LED headlight, a 5-inch LCD digital instrument cluster, telescopic front forks, and a Combi-Braking System (CBS) paired with a 220 mm front disc brake.

The QJ Motor FORT 600 2026 is a mid-displacement maxi-scooter designed for high-performance city commuting and long-distance touring. It features a 550cc liquid-cooled, 8-valve, two-cylinder engine that produces roughly 53.7 hp (39.5 kW) at 7,500 rpm and 54 Nm of torque at 5,750 rpm. With a curb weight of 215 kg and a 14-liter fuel tank, the FORT 600 offers stable highway cruising while maintaining an agile 750 mm seat height. Equipped with dual-disc brakes with ABS, an upside-down front fork, and wide tubeless tires, this maxi-scooter combines premium comfort, sharp styling, and practical everyday performance.

Triumph Bonneville T40
The newly unveiled Triumph Bonneville T40 2027 brings the classic Bonneville design to Triumph’s smaller-capacity range, combining traditional styling with a modern single-cylinder engine. In markets outside India, the T40 is powered by Triumph’s 398cc liquid-cooled, single-cylinder TR-Series engine, giving it a stronger performance focus while maintaining the relaxed character expected from a Bonneville. The engine is paired with a six-speed gearbox and is tuned to deliver useful low- and mid-range torque for everyday riding. Its styling stays true to Triumph’s classic roadster design, featuring a round headlight, sculpted fuel tank, spoke-style wheels, twin rear shocks, a long seat, and a traditional exhaust. At the same time, modern rider aids and electronic features bring the bike up to date without taking away from its retro appearance, making the T40 a blend of classic Bonneville character and contemporary technology.
For India, Triumph uses a smaller 350cc version of the engine instead of the 398cc unit offered in other markets. This India-spec 350cc engine is designed specifically for the local market and produces around 29 hp and 31 Nm of torque, paired with a six-speed transmission. The Indian-spec T40 also comes with modern features such as ride-by-wire, multiple riding modes, traction control, cornering ABS, cruise control, and a colour TFT instrument display, depending on the final specification. With its smaller engine, the India-market T40 offers a more accessible entry into the Bonneville family while retaining the classic styling and character associated with Triumph.
Triumph Bonneville T40 Black
The Triumph Bonneville T40 Black is the darker and more distinctive version of the T40, using the same basic mechanical package while adding a more aggressive visual treatment. It retains the traditional Bonneville proportions, including the round headlight, teardrop-style fuel tank, spoke wheels, twin rear suspension, and classic exhaust layout. However, several components receive darker finishes, giving the Black model a more premium and muscular appearance. In international markets, the T40 Black is powered by the 398cc single-cylinder TR-Series engine, which offers a good balance of everyday usability and performance. The six-speed transmission and modern electronic features also make it well suited to both urban riding and longer weekend trips.
The Indian version uses Triumph’s 350cc engine instead of the 398cc motor offered in other markets. This India-specific engine produces approximately 29 hp and 31 Nm of torque, giving the T40 Black performance suited to the 350cc category while maintaining the same overall Bonneville character. The Indian model combines its classic design with modern equipment, including riding modes, ride-by-wire, traction control, cornering ABS, cruise control, and a full-colour TFT display. Darker finishes across the engine and bodywork, along with contrasting details, give the T40 Black a more distinctive appearance than the standard T40 without changing the motorcycle’s core character.
Triumph Bonneville T4
The Triumph Bonneville T4 is positioned as a more affordable and straightforward member of Triumph’s smaller-capacity Bonneville family. It follows the same retro-roadster design theme, with a classic fuel tank, round headlight, spoke wheels, twin rear shocks, and a traditional exhaust. However, its equipment and overall specification are focused on keeping the motorcycle more accessible. In international markets, the T4 uses Triumph’s 398cc liquid-cooled, single-cylinder engine, giving it more displacement than the India-specific version. The engine is paired with a six-speed gearbox and is designed to provide useful torque for both city riding and open-road journeys, while the relaxed riding position and classic chassis complement its Bonneville-inspired character.
For the Indian market, however, the Bonneville T4 gets a 350cc version of Triumph’s single-cylinder engine. The India-spec motor produces roughly 29 hp and 31 Nm of torque and is paired with a six-speed gearbox. Triumph has effectively tailored the engine capacity to suit the Indian market while keeping the overall Bonneville concept intact. Compared with the T40, the T4 places greater emphasis on affordability and straightforward equipment, making it a more accessible entry point into Triumph’s Bonneville range. This gives Indian buyers a genuine Bonneville-style motorcycle with a 350cc engine, while customers in other markets receive the larger 398cc version.

Description:
The Kawasaki Z300 2027 is an accessible streetfighter that combines aggressive naked-bike styling with the performance of a proven parallel-twin engine. Drawing design inspiration from its larger Z-series siblings, such as the Z900, the Z300 features sharp, Sugomi-inspired bodywork, a muscular fuel tank, and an upright riding position suited to urban commuting and spirited weekend rides.
Power comes from a 296cc, liquid-cooled, parallel-twin engine that produces approximately 40 bhp and 26.3 Nm of torque, paired with a six-speed gearbox and an assist-and-slipper clutch for smoother gear changes. A lightweight chassis, disc brakes, and dual-channel ABS on equipped versions contribute to confident handling and braking performance. The Z300 delivers a distinctive high-revving twin-cylinder character, making it an appealing alternative to single-cylinder rivals for riders seeking sporty performance in an approachable naked-bike package.
specs: OVERALL DIMENSIONS (L X W X H)

Description:
The newly unveiled Aprilia SXR GT 175 2027 brings a sharper maxi-scooter aesthetic and performance updates aimed at urban commuters and highway tourers alike. As the latest addition to Aprilia’s maxi-style scooter lineup, it features aggressive bodywork with GT-inspired footboard graphics, a redesigned windscreen, and a signature tripod LED headlight setup.
Powering the scooter is a BS6 OBD II Stage B-compliant 174.7 cc, single-cylinder, air-cooled, 3-valve engine that produces 13.09 bhp at 7,200 rpm and 14.14 Nm of torque at 6,000 rpm. To enhance stability and long-distance comfort, it rides on larger 14-inch alloy wheels.
Standard features include a 5-inch TFT instrument console with Bluetooth connectivity, turn-by-turn navigation, and dedicated handlebar controls. Braking is handled by a 220 mm front disc brake paired with single-channel ABS.

The Honda CGX 150 2026 stands out as a distinctive addition to Honda’s motorcycle lineup, blending classic cafe-racer styling with dependable, modern engineering. Inspired by mid-20th-century road-racing heritage, the motorcycle immediately catches the eye with its vintage design cues, including a classic round LED headlight, a sculpted fuel tank, bar-end mirrors, a ribbed tuck-and-roll bench seat, and traditional spoked wheels. Beneath its retro-inspired styling lies a 149cc, air-cooled, single-cylinder, four-stroke engine paired with a smooth five-speed transmission, tuned to deliver responsive low- to mid-range torque for an engaging and practical urban riding experience. Modern features, such as front and rear disc brakes, ABS options, inverted front forks, dual rear shock absorbers, and a digital-analog instrument display, aim to enhance safety, stability, and convenience without compromising its retro character. Lightweight, nimble, and fuel-efficient, the Honda CGX 150 bridges the gap between everyday commuting and lifestyle riding, offering enthusiasts a stylish, factory-built roadster with an accessible design and plenty of personality.

Model_Site: FAT BOY (All-Terrain Fat Tire Electric Bike)
Description:
The Yadea FAT BOY is a robust, premium all-terrain electric bike designed to handle everything from city streets to sand, snow, and rugged off-road trails. Equipped with ultra-wide 20 × 4.5-inch fat tires, dual suspension, and a plush saddle, it absorbs bumps and shocks to deliver a stable and comfortable ride across various surfaces.
At its core, the FAT BOY features a powerful 750W rear hub motor paired with a responsive torque sensor and a Shimano 8-speed drivetrain. This combination provides smooth, natural pedal assistance and ample power to tackle steep hills. Safety and control are enhanced by high-performance hydraulic disc brakes, delivering reliable stopping power in various weather and riding conditions.
Blending a bold, scrambler-inspired design with practical features such as a dropper seatpost and dual suspension, the Yadea FAT BOY stands out as a versatile, adventure-ready e-bike for leisure riders and outdoor enthusiasts alike.
specs: Eco / Pedal-Assist Mode: Up to 140 km (~87 miles)
Pure Throttle / High Power Assist: Approx. 60 - 80 km
Throttle / Multi-Level Pedal Assist (PAS) / Shimano 8-Speed Drivetrain
Front and Rear Hydraulic Disc Brakes
Dual Suspension (Front Suspension Fork + Rear Shock Absorbers)

Description:
The newly launched Bajaj Pulsar N250 SS 2026 brings significant performance, technology, and electronic upgrades to Bajaj’s quarter-litre streetfighter lineup. At its heart is an upgraded 249cc, single-cylinder, four-valve, oil-cooled engine, paired with a new six-speed gearbox that replaces the previous five-speed unit, along with a bidirectional quickshifter marketed as the Sports Shifter. The engine produces 25 PS of power and 22 Nm of torque, promising a more engaging and responsive riding experience.
On the technology front, the N250 SS features a 5-inch TFT color display with Google Maps turn-by-turn navigation, Bluetooth connectivity, call and SMS alerts, and document storage. Rider control and safety are further enhanced by ride-by-wire throttle technology, four riding modes (Road, Rain, Sport, and Off-road), adjustable brake and clutch levers, dual-channel ABS, traction control, and panic brake alerts. The motorcycle is also available in four new color schemes: Atlantic Blue, Brooklyn Black, Fiery Red Orange, and Pearl Metallic White, giving its updated streetfighter styling a fresh and distinctive look.

The Benelli TRK 552X 2026 brings significant upgrades to the middleweight adventure-touring segment, replacing the popular TRK 502X with improved performance, modern technology, and enhanced touring comfort. At its heart is an upgraded 554cc, liquid-cooled, parallel-twin engine producing approximately 52 bhp of maximum power and 49 Nm of torque, delivering stronger performance for highway cruising and adventure riding.
Designed for riders who enjoy exploring beyond paved roads, the TRK 552X features 19-inch front and 17-inch rear cross-spoke wheels, 50mm Marzocchi upside-down (USD) front forks, 210mm of ground clearance, and an 860mm seat height. Its rugged styling is complemented by a tubular steel trellis frame and an aluminium swingarm. Modern features include full LED lighting, a 5-inch TFT instrument display with Bluetooth connectivity and navigation, a Tyre Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS), heated grips, and a heated rider seat for added comfort on long journeys. A 20-litre fuel tank, Bosch dual-channel ABS, and enhanced touring equipment further strengthen its appeal. Combining adventure-ready hardware with practical technology, the Benelli TRK 552X is designed for riders seeking a versatile, full-sized adventure tourer for long-distance travel and light off-road exploration.
specs: Tubular trellis frame with aluminium swingarm

Description: The Honda NXR 160 Bros 2027 is a versatile dual-purpose motorcycle featuring rugged, trail-inspired styling. Developed primarily for Latin American markets, it has become one of Honda’s popular models in the region. It is powered by a reliable 162.7cc, air-cooled, single-cylinder OHC engine with PGM-FI electronic fuel injection, producing 10.4 kW at 8,000 rpm on gasoline and 10.5 kW at 8,000 rpm on ethanol. Maximum torque stands at 14.1 Nm at 5,500 rpm on gasoline and 14.2 Nm at 5,500 rpm on ethanol, paired with a five-speed transmission. Designed for both busy urban streets and rough rural roads, the motorcycle features a high-mounted front mudguard, long-travel telescopic front forks, a rear monoshock, and dual-purpose tires mounted on 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheels. Its generous 247 mm ground clearance and upright riding position make it a practical choice for daily commuting and riding on unpaved terrain. The 2027 model also features LED lighting and is available in versions equipped with either a Combined Braking System (CBS) or an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), depending on the variant. Other practical features and equipment may vary by version and market.
